title.zh: 卷二十四 魏書二十四 韓崔高孫王傳
title.en: Volume 24: Book of Wei 24 - Biographies of Han, Cui, Gao, Sun, and Wang
title.raw: 卷二十四 魏書二十四 韓崔高孫王傳 Volume 24: Book of Wei 24 - Biographies of Han, Cui, Gao, Sun, and Wang

sentences.zh: 韓曁 崔林 高柔 孫禮 王觀

translations.literal: Han Ji, Cui Lin, Gao Rou, Sun Li, and Wang Guan.
translations.idiomatic: This volume records Han Ji, Cui Lin, Gao Rou, Sun Li, and Wang Guan.

sentences.zh: 韓曁字公至，南陽堵陽人也。

translations.literal: Han Ji, courtesy name Gongzhi, was a man of Duyang in Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji, whose courtesy name was Gongzhi, came from Duyang in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《楚國先賢傳》曰：曁，韓王信之後。

translations.literal: 〈The Chu guo xianxian zhuan says: Ji was a descendant of King Xin of Han.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of the Chu Region states that Han Ji was a descendant of King Xin of Han.

sentences.zh: 祖術，河東太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shu was Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Han Shu had served as Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父純，南郡太守。〉

translations.literal: His father Chun was Administrator of Nan commandery.〉
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Chun had served as Administrator of Nan commandery.〉

sentences.zh: 同縣豪右陳茂，譖曁父兄，幾至大辟。

translations.literal: A powerful local magnate of the same county, Chen Mao, slandered Ji's father and elder brothers, so that they nearly suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mao, a wealthy bully in the same county, denounced Han Ji's father and brothers until they stood on the edge of the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 曁陽不以為言，庸賃積資，陰結死士，遂追呼尋禽茂，以首祭父墓，由是顯名。

translations.literal: Ji outwardly spoke nothing of it, hired himself out for wages to amass funds, secretly gathered men willing to die for him, then pursued, called out, sought, and captured Mao, and with Mao's head sacrificed at his father's grave; by this he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji kept his own counsel, took day labor to scrape together money, and quietly recruited loyal followers until he could hunt Chen Mao down, kill him, and offer the man's head at his father's tomb—an act that made his name known far and wide.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，司空辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt, and the Minister of Works summoned him; he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt and summoned by the Minister of Works, he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 乃變名姓，隱居避亂魯陽山中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he changed his name and surname, and lived in reclusion in the mountains of Luyang to escape turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He then changed his name, withdrew into the Luyang hills, and sat out the chaos in hiding.

sentences.zh: 山民合黨，欲行寇掠。

translations.literal: The mountain people banded together in factions and wished to carry out raiding and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: The hill folk formed armed bands and were bent on pillage.

sentences.zh: 曁散家財以供牛酒，請其渠帥，為陳安危。

translations.literal: Ji scattered his household wealth to supply oxen and wine, invited their chieftains, and for them set forth what was safe and what was perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji spent his family fortune on feasts of beef and wine, invited their leaders, and patiently explained the stakes—safety against ruin.

sentences.zh: 山民化之，終不為害。

translations.literal: The mountain people were transformed by him and in the end did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: They took his counsel to heart and never carried out their raids.

sentences.zh: 避袁術命召，徙居山都之山。

translations.literal: Avoiding Yuan Shu's orders and summons, he moved his residence to the mountains of Shandu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu tried to conscript him, he moved deeper into the Shandu range to stay out of reach.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表禮辟，遂遁逃，南居孱陵界，所在見敬愛，而表深恨之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Jingzhou, Liu Biao, courteously summoned him; he thereupon fled, and dwelt south on the border of Zangling, where wherever he went he was seen with respect and love, while Biao deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao, Governor of Jingzhou, courted him with a formal summons; Han Ji slipped away instead and settled south along the Zangling frontier, where commoners and gentry alike admired him—which only deepened Liu Biao's grudge.

sentences.zh: 曁懼，應命，除宜城長。

translations.literal: Ji was afraid, answered the summons, and was appointed Magistrate of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed at last, he answered the call and accepted appointment as magistrate of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖平荊州，辟為丞相士曹屬。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Jingzhou, he was summoned as an aide in the Minister of Works' personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao conquered Jingzhou, Han Ji was recruited as an aide in the personnel bureau of the Chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 後選樂陵太守，徙監冶謁者。

translations.literal: Later he was selected as Administrator of Leling, and transferred to be the metallurgy overseer.
translations.idiomatic: He was later chosen Administrator of Leling, then reassigned to supervise the imperial foundries.

sentences.zh: 舊時冶，作馬排，

translations.literal: In former times at the smelting works, they used horse-driven bellows (pai),
translations.idiomatic: The old practice at the ironworks was to drive the bellows with teams of horses.

sentences.zh: 〈蒲拜反。

translations.literal: 〈The reading is "bai" after 蒲 (pu-bai fan).〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The commentary glosses the character with the fanqie spelling pu-bai.〉

sentences.zh: 為排以吹炭。〉

translations.literal: They made a pai to blow the charcoal.〉
translations.idiomatic: A "pai" was a set of bellows to fan the furnace coals.〉

sentences.zh: 每一熟石用馬百匹；

translations.literal: For each "cooked" stone they used a hundred horses;
translations.idiomatic: Each batch of ore smelted through consumed the strength of a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 更作人排，又費功力；

translations.literal: when they switched to human-powered bellows, it again wasted labor power;
translations.idiomatic: Switching to manpower was just as wasteful of labor.

sentences.zh: 曁乃因長流為水排，計其利益，三倍於前。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon used the long current to make water-driven bellows, and reckoning their profit, it was three times what it had been before.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji harnessed a swift stream to power water bellows; the output and savings tripled compared with the old methods.

sentences.zh: 在職七年，器用充實。

translations.literal: In office seven years, tools and supplies were ample and solid.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in that post left the arsenals and workshops abundantly stocked.

sentences.zh: 制書襃歎，就加司金都尉，班亞九卿。

translations.literal: An edict in imperial script praised him, and he was thereupon promoted to Director of Metals, with rank just below the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued a written commendation and added the title Director of Metals for the Court of Wei, a post that ranked just below the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，封宜城亭侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne, Han Ji received the village marquisate of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 黃初七年，遷太常，進封南鄉亭侯，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangchu, he was promoted to Grand Master of Ceremonies, advanced to village marquis of Nanxiang, with two hundred households in his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 7 he rose to Grand Master of Ceremonies and was promoted to village marquis of Nanxiang with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時新都洛陽，制度未備，而宗廟主祏

translations.literal: At that time the new capital was Luoyang, the institutions were not yet complete, and the ancestral temple spirit tablets (zhu shi)
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang was still being built into a capital, its ritual framework unfinished, and the spirit tablets for the dynastic temple—

sentences.zh: 〈祏音石。

translations.literal: 〈shi is read like "shi" (stone).
translations.idiomatic: 〈The character 祏 is glossed with the same sound as 石 (stone).〉

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：命我先人典司宗祏。

translations.literal: The Zuo zhuan says: "He ordered my forebears to be in charge of the ancestral tablets (zong shi).
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition records the charge, "He bade my ancestors keep custody of the royal tablets in the ancestral shrine."

sentences.zh: 注曰：「宗廟所以藏主石室者。」〉

translations.literal: The commentary note says: "That in the ancestral temple by which the spirit tablets are stored in the stone chamber."〉
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains: the stone chamber within the great temple where the wooden spirit tablets rest.〉

sentences.zh: 皆在鄴都。

translations.literal: were all at the old capital in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: —still lay at the old capital in Ye.

sentences.zh: 曁奏請迎鄴四廟神主，建立洛陽廟，四時蒸嘗，親奉粢盛。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized requesting to welcome the spirit lords of Ye's four shrines, establish a Luoyang temple, and for the four seasonal offerings personally present the grain offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji petitioned to bring the four sets of ancestral tablets down from Ye, install them in a new temple at Luoyang, and personally tend the seasonal grain offerings year round.

sentences.zh: 崇明正禮，廢去淫祀，多所匡正。

translations.literal: He exalted and clarified correct ritual, abolished excessive cults, and in many matters corrected deviations.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted orthodox rites, swept away illegitimate local cults, and straightened out a host of ritual abuses.

sentences.zh: 在官八年，以疾遜位。

translations.literal: In office eight years, he yielded his position on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in that office ill health forced him to retire.

sentences.zh: 景初二年春，詔曰：「太中大夫韓曁，澡身浴德，志節高絜，年踰八十，守道彌固，可謂純篤，老而益劭者也。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Jingchu, an edict said: "Grand Counselor Han Ji has bathed his person in virtue, his purpose and integrity are lofty and pure, he is past eighty yet holds to the Way all the firmer—he may be called sincere and staunch, old yet ever more vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jingchu 2 an edict declared: "Grand Counselor Han Ji has purified himself in virtue; his resolve stands high and unsullied. Past eighty, he clings to the Way more firmly than ever—utterly steadfast, growing stronger in age."

sentences.zh: 其以曁為司徒。

translations.literal: Let Ji be made Minister of Education."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be appointed Minister of Education."

sentences.zh: 」夏四月薨，遺令歛以時服，葬為土藏。

translations.literal: "In summer, fourth month, he died; his final instructions were to be shrouded in timely dress and buried in an earthen vault.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of summer, leaving orders for a plain shroud and a simple earth-chamber burial.

sentences.zh: 謚曰恭侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Marquis Gong ("the reverent").

sentences.zh: 〈《楚國先賢傳》曰：曁臨終遺言曰：「夫俗奢者，示之以儉，儉則節之以禮。

translations.literal: 〈The Chu guo xianxian zhuan says: on the verge of death Ji's testamentary words said: "Where custom is extravagant, show them frugality; where there is frugality, restrain it with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Traditions of Worthies of the Chu Region records his deathbed words: "When the age grows wasteful, teach restraint; when men turn miserly, bring them back with ritual.

sentences.zh: 歷見前代送終過制，失之甚矣。

translations.literal: I have seen past generations' funeral practices exceed regulation; the error is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched generation after generation outdo one another in lavish funerals—the excess is unbearable.

sentences.zh: 若爾曹敬聽吾言，斂以時服，葬以土藏，穿畢便葬，送以瓦器，慎勿有增益。

translations.literal: If you respectfully heed my words, shroud me in timely dress, bury me in an earthen vault, dig the pit and bury at once, send me off with pottery vessels, carefully do not add anything beyond."
translations.idiomatic: If you sons truly honor me, wrap my body in everyday clothes, lay me in a plain earth pit, fill it in at once, and send me off with nothing costlier than coarse pottery—nothing extra on the bier."

sentences.zh: 」又上疏曰：「生有益於民，死猶不害於民。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial saying: "In life I benefited the people; in death I still should not harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also forwarded a memorial: "I tried in life to burden the people as little as possible; I will not burden them in death.

sentences.zh: 況臣備位台司，在職日淺，未能宣揚聖德以廣益黎庶。

translations.literal: Moreover I occupy a place among the Three Excellencies, my days in office have been short, and I have been unable to spread abroad the sage virtue to broadly benefit the black-haired folk.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have sat among the Three Excellencies too briefly to broadcast the sovereign's kindness to the common folk.

sentences.zh: 寢疾彌留，奄即幽冥。

translations.literal: My illness lingers on the brink; suddenly I go to the dark world.
translations.idiomatic: My sickness has reached its final stage; I am about to cross into the shades.

sentences.zh: 方今百姓農務，不宜勞役，乞不令洛陽吏民供設喪具。

translations.literal: At present the hundred surnames are busy with farm work; it is not fitting to trouble them with corvée; I beg that the officials and people of Luoyang not be ordered to supply funeral equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The farmers are in the thick of spring work; do not drag the households of Luoyang into mourning levies for my sake.

sentences.zh: 懼國典有常，使臣私願不得展從，謹冒以聞，惟蒙哀許。

translations.literal: I fear the state regulations have their constant forms, so that my private wish cannot be carried through; I venture to risk offense in reporting this, only hoping compassionately to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: State ritual may have its rules, yet I beg you to waive them this once so my last wish may be honored—I lay this before you in hope of mercy."

sentences.zh: 」帝得表嗟歎，乃詔曰：「故司徒韓曁，積德履行，忠以立朝，至於黃髮，直亮不虧。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the memorial he sighed in admiration, and thereupon issued an edict saying: "The late Minister of Education Han Ji, accumulating virtue and practicing conduct, was loyal in serving the court; reaching hoary hair, he was straight and bright without fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the plea and sighed with admiration, then replied: "The late Minister of Education Han Ji built his life on integrity; his loyalty shone in court service, and even in white hairs he never bent.

sentences.zh: 旣登三事，望獲毗輔之助，如何奄忽，天命不永！

translations.literal: Having ascended to the Three Affairs, we hoped to obtain the help of assisting and supporting; how could he suddenly pass away—Heaven's mandate is not long!
translations.idiomatic: We raised him among the Three Excellencies expecting his counsel—how cruel that Heaven cut him off so soon!"

sentences.zh: 曾參臨沒，易簀以禮；

translations.literal: When Zeng Shen was near death, he changed the mat in accordance with ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Zengzi on his deathbed exchanged his fine mat for a humble one, as ritual demanded;

sentences.zh: 晏嬰尚儉，遣車降制。

translations.literal: Yan Ying esteemed frugality and sent down the number of funeral carts to match regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying insisted on thrift and trimmed the funeral train to what the rites allowed.

sentences.zh: 今司徒知命，遺言卹民，必欲崇約，可謂善始令終者也。

translations.literal: Now the Minister of Education, knowing Heaven's command, left testamentary words showing compassion for the people, and was determined to honor austerity—he may be called one who had a good beginning and a good end.
translations.idiomatic: Our Minister of Education, knowing his end was near, thought first of sparing the people and clung to simplicity—here was a man who began well and finished well.

sentences.zh: 其喪禮所設，皆如故事，勿有所闕。

translations.literal: As for the funeral rites to be set out, let all be according to precedent; do not let there be any lack."
translations.idiomatic: Conduct the state funeral by the book; let nothing be omitted that precedent requires."

sentences.zh: 」時賜溫明祕器，衣一稱，五時朝服，玉具劒佩。〉

translations.literal: At that time there was granted the warm-bright secret coffin, one suit of clothes, five-season court dress, and a jade-mounted sword and belt pendant.〉
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless the court still sent the lacquered "warm-bright" inner coffin, a full set of robes, court dress for each season, and a jade-hilted sword with fittings.〉

sentences.zh: 子肇嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han Zhao succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 肇薨，子邦嗣。

translations.literal: When Zhao died, his son Bang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Zhao died, his son Han Bang inherited.

sentences.zh: 〈《楚國先賢傳》曰：邦字長林。

translations.literal: 〈The Chu guo xianxian zhuan says: Bang's courtesy name was Changlin.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The same tradition gives Han Bang the courtesy name Changlin.

sentences.zh: 少有才學。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he showed literary and scholarly gifts.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝時為野王令，有稱績。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Jin he was Magistrate of Yewang, and had a reputation for administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Wudi he served as magistrate of Yewang and earned praise for his governance.

sentences.zh: 為新城太守，坐舉野王故吏為新城計吏，武帝大怒，遂殺邦。

translations.literal: He became Administrator of Xincheng, and because he recommended a former subordinate of Yewang as Xincheng's clerk of accounts, Emperor Wu was greatly angered and thereupon executed Bang.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Administrator of Xincheng, he nominated an old Yewang clerk to be county accountant; the emperor took this as a breach of rules and had Han Bang put to death.

sentences.zh: 曁次子繇，高陽太守。

translations.literal: Ji's second son You was Administrator of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji's second son Han You became Administrator of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 繇子洪，侍御史。

translations.literal: You's son Hong was Palace Assistant Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Han You's son Han Hong rose to imperial secretary.

sentences.zh: 洪子壽，字德貞。

translations.literal: Hong's son Shou, courtesy name Dezhen.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong's son Han Shou bore the courtesy name Dezhen.

sentences.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：自曁已下，世治素業，壽能敦尚家風，性尤忠厚。

translations.literal: The Jin zhugong zan says: From Ji downward, generations managed plain occupations; Shou was able to honor and esteem the family style, and his nature was especially honest and generous.
translations.idiomatic: The Appraisal of Jin Ministers remarks that from Han Ji onward the family pursued modest callings; Han Shou upheld that tradition and was noted for his frank, generous temper.

sentences.zh: 早歷清職，惠帝踐阼，為散騎常侍，遷守河南尹。

translations.literal: Early he passed through pure offices; when Emperor Hui ascended the throne, he became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and was transferred to acting Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early through unsullied posts; when Emperor Hui mounted the throne he entered the palace as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and later acted as governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 病卒，贈驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He died of illness; posthumously he was awarded General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously named General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 壽妻賈充女。

translations.literal: Shou's wife was a daughter of Jia Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shou had married a daughter of Jia Chong.

sentences.zh: 充無後，以壽子謐為嗣，弱冠為祕書監侍中，性驕佚而才出壽。

translations.literal: Chong had no posterity, and took Shou's son Mi as heir; at the capping age he became Director of the Palace Library and Attendant-in-Ordinary; his nature was arrogant and dissolute while his talent exceeded Shou's.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong had no sons, so he adopted Han Shou's boy Han Mi as heir; still in his twenties Mi became director of the palace library and attendant-in-ordinary—brilliant but arrogant, and cleverer than his father.

sentences.zh: 少子蔚，亦有器望，並為趙王倫所誅。

translations.literal: The younger son Wei also had capacity and reputation, and both were executed by Prince Zhao of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: A younger son, Han Wei, was equally promising, yet Prince Sima Lun of Zhao executed both brothers.

sentences.zh: 韓氏遂滅。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon the Han clan was extinguished.〉
translations.idiomatic: With that the house of Han came to an end.〉

sentences.zh: 崔林字德儒，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Lin, courtesy name Deru, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin, courtesy name Deru, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 少時晚成，宗族莫知，惟從兄琰異之。

translations.literal: In youth he matured late; the lineage kin knew nothing of him, only his elder cousin Yan thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was a late bloomer as a boy, ignored by his kinsmen until his cousin Cui Yan singled him out as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 太祖定兾州，召除鄔長，貧無車馬，單步之官。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Jizhou, he was summoned and appointed Magistrate of Wu; poor, without carriage or horse, he went to his post on foot alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao conquered Jizhou, Cui Lin was called up as magistrate of Wu; too poor to afford a mount, he walked to his post alone.

sentences.zh: 太祖征壺關，問長吏德政最者，并州刺史張陟以林對，於是擢為兾州主簿，徙署別駕、丞相掾屬。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Huguan, he asked which county magistrate's virtuous government was foremost; the Inspector of Bingzhou, Zhang Zhi, answered with Lin, whereupon he was promoted to Chief Clerk of Jizhou, transferred to acting Chief Clerk on the staff, and aide in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huguan campaign Cao Cao asked which local magistrate governed best; Bingzhou Inspector Zhang Zhi named Cui Lin, who was promptly elevated to chief clerk of Jizhou, then shifted to chief clerk on staff and aide in the Chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 魏國旣建，稍遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was established, he was gradually promoted to Palace Assistant Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the kingdom of Wei was founded he rose step by step to palace assistant secretary.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，拜尚書，出為幽州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was appointed Master of Writing, and went out as Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne Cui Lin became a Master of Writing, then left the capital as Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 北中郎將吳質統河北軍事，涿郡太守王雄謂林別駕曰：「吳中郎將，上所親重，國之貴臣也。

translations.literal: The General of the North Center, Wu Zhi, commanded Hebei military affairs; the Administrator of Zhuo commandery, Wang Xiong, said to Lin's chief clerk: "The General of the North Center is one whom the Sovereign personally esteems, a noble minister of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhi, General of the North Center, held military authority over Hebei. Zhuo Administrator Wang Xiong warned Cui Lin's chief clerk: "Wu Zhi is a favorite of the throne and a pillar of the court.

sentences.zh: 杖節統事，州郡莫不奉牋致敬，而崔使君初不與相聞。

translations.literal: Bearing the staff of office he manages affairs; no prefecture or commandery fails to submit letters paying respect, yet Cui the Inspector from the beginning has not communicated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He wields the imperial baton—every province sends him respectful letters—yet your Inspector Cui has never so much as called on him.

sentences.zh: 若以邊塞不脩斬卿，使君寧能護卿邪？

translations.literal: If on the grounds that the border defenses are not repaired he beheads you, can the Inspector protect you?"
translations.idiomatic: If he decides the frontier works are neglected and orders your execution, do you imagine Cui Lin will shield you?"

sentences.zh: 」別駕具以白林，林曰：「刺史視去此州如脫屣，寧當相累邪？

translations.literal: The chief clerk reported everything to Lin; Lin said: "The Inspector looks on leaving this province as like slipping off a shoe—how could he drag you down with him?
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk relayed the threat. Cui Lin replied: "I would leave this province as lightly as kicking off a sandal—why would I let his bullying implicate you?

sentences.zh: 此州與胡虜接，宜鎮之以靜，擾之則動其逆心，特為國家生北顧憂，以此為寄。

translations.literal: This province borders the Hu barbarians; it should be quieted with calm; if disturbed, it will stir their rebellious hearts, and specially for the state give birth to the worry of looking north—this is what I entrust to you."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou fronts the steppe; it must be governed with calm. Provoke Wu Zhi and you rouse the tribes—nothing but fresh trouble on the northern frontier. That is what truly worries me."

sentences.zh: 」在官一期，寇竊寢息；

translations.literal: In office one full year, raiding and theft gradually ceased;
translations.idiomatic: Within a single tour of duty banditry faded to nothing.

sentences.zh: 〈案《王氏譜》：雄字元伯，太保祥之宗也。

translations.literal: 〈According to the Wang shi pu: Xiong's courtesy name was Yuanbo, of the same lineage as Grand Guardian Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wang clan genealogy identifies Wang Xiong, style Yuanbo, as kin to Grand Guardian Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 《魏名臣奏》載安定太守孟達薦雄曰：「臣聞明君以求賢為業，忠臣以進善為效，故易稱『拔茅連茹』，傳曰『舉爾所知』。

translations.literal: The Wei mingchen zou records that the Administrator of Anding, Meng Da, recommended Xiong, saying: "I have heard that the enlightened ruler takes seeking worthies as his task, and the loyal minister takes advancing the good as his service; therefore the Changes speaks of "pulling up the mao, its roots connected," and the tradition says "promote those whom you know."
translations.idiomatic: The Memorials of Wei Notables preserves Meng Da, Administrator of Anding, recommending Wang Xiong: "A wise sovereign wins the realm by seeking talent; a loyal minister repays favor by lifting the worthy. The Zhou yi speaks of pulling a single reed and drawing the whole clump; the Analects tell a ruler to promote men he truly knows."

sentences.zh: 臣不自量，竊慕其義。

translations.literal: I do not measure myself, but privately admire its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I hardly match that standard, yet I admire the principle.

sentences.zh: 臣昔以人乏，謬充備部職。

translations.literal: Formerly, because men were lacking, I wrongly filled a post in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when offices stood empty, I overstayed my turn in the clerical ranks.

sentences.zh: 時涿郡太守王雄為西部從事，與臣同僚。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Xiong, Administrator of Zhuo commandery, was a western-section clerk and served in the same office as your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong of Zhuo then served as a western-section clerk alongside me.

sentences.zh: 雄天性良固，果而有謀。

translations.literal: Xiong's natural disposition was good and firm, decisive yet with planning.
translations.idiomatic: His nature is steady and resolute, bold yet thoughtful.

sentences.zh: 歷試三縣，政成人和。

translations.literal: He was tested in three counties, and government was accomplished and people harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Trials in three counties left good order and contented people.

sentences.zh: 及在近職，奉宣威恩，懷柔有術，清慎持法。

translations.literal: When he reached a nearby office, he proclaimed awe-inspiring favor, soothed and cherished with method, was pure and cautious in upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: Closer to court he spread imperial majesty with tact, soothed the people, and enforced the code with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 臣往年出使，經過雄郡。

translations.literal: In former years when your subject went out on mission, he passed through Xiong's commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy last year I traveled through his district.

sentences.zh: 自說特受陛下拔擢之恩，常勵節精心，思投命為效。

translations.literal: He himself said he had received the grace of being specially lifted up by Your Majesty, and constantly urged his integrity and refined his mind, thinking to devote his life to repay the effect.
translations.idiomatic: He told me how deeply he valued Your Majesty's personal promotion and swore to polish his integrity and lay down his life in your service.

sentences.zh: 言辭激揚，情趣款惻。

translations.literal: His words were ardent and stirring, his mood sincere and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: His voice shook with feeling; there was no mistaking his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚闇，不識真偽，以謂雄才兼資文武，忠烈之性，踰越倫輩。

translations.literal: Your subject, though foolish and dim, does not recognize truth and falsehood, but considers that Xiong's talents combine civil and martial endowment, and his loyal and ardent nature surpasses his peers.
translations.idiomatic: I am no judge of fine distinctions, yet I see in him both civil talent and military grit, with a loyalty fiercer than most of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 今涿郡領戶三千，孤寡之家，參居其半，北有守兵藩衞之固，誠不足舒雄智力，展其勤幹也。

translations.literal: Now Zhuo commandery registers three thousand households; orphaned and widowed households, mixed in, are half of them; north there are garrison troops and the solidity of screen and guard—it is truly insufficient to relax Xiong's intelligence and strength, and display his diligent capability.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo today counts only three thousand households, half of them widows and orphans under garrison protection—hardly enough scope to stretch Wang Xiong's abilities.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩深厚，無以報國，不勝慺慺淺見之情，謹冒陳聞。

translations.literal: Your subject has received deep favor and has no means to repay the state; unable to overcome my shallow feelings of earnest loyalty, I venture to risk offense in laying this before you.
translations.idiomatic: I owe the dynasty too much to stay silent; forgive this blunt memorial born of gratitude."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「昔蕭何薦韓信，鄧禹進吳漢，惟賢知賢也。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Formerly Xiao He recommended Han Xin, and Deng Yu advanced Wu Han—only the worthy recognize the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "Xiao He once lifted Han Xin; Deng Yu raised Wu Han—talent knows talent.

sentences.zh: 雄有膽智技能文武之姿，吾宿知之。

translations.literal: Xiong has courage, wisdom, and the bearing of combining civil and martial; I have long known him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong has courage, wit, and both book and sword—I have watched him for years.

sentences.zh: 今便以參散騎之選，方使少在吾門下知指歸，便大用之矣。

translations.literal: Now immediately let him join the selection for Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; for the moment let him serve a short while at my gate and know the guiding principles, then he will be greatly used.
translations.idiomatic: Enroll him at once among the attendants-in-ordinary; let him study court usage at my side awhile, then give him a weightier post.

sentences.zh: 天下之士，欲使皆先歷散騎，然後出據州郡，是吾本意也。

translations.literal: As for the scholars of the realm, I wish them all first to pass through Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then go out to occupy prefectures and commanderies—this is my original intention."
translations.idiomatic: I want every promising man in the empire to serve first as attendant-in-ordinary before he is sent to a provincial seat—that has always been my design."

sentences.zh: 」雄後為幽州刺史。

translations.literal: 〉Later Xiong became Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 〉Wang Xiong was later promoted to Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子渾，涼州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Hun was Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Hun became Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 次乂，平北將軍。

translations.literal: The next son Yi was General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Wang Yi rose to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 司徒安豐侯戎，渾之子。

translations.literal: Minister of Education and Marquis of Anfeng Rong was Hun's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong—the future Minister of Education and Marquis of Anfeng—was Wang Hun's son.

sentences.zh: 太尉武陵侯衍、荊州刺史澄，皆乂之子。〉

translations.literal: Grand Commandant and Marquis of Wuling Yan, and Inspector of Jingzhou Cheng, were both sons of Yi.〉
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan, Marquis of Wuling, and Wang Cheng, who governed Jingzhou, were both sons of Wang Yi.〉

sentences.zh: 猶以不事上司，左遷河間太守，清論多為林怨也。

translations.literal: Still, because he did not attend to his superior, he was demoted to Administrator of Hejian, and the "pure critics" for the most part bore resentment against Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin was nonetheless demoted to Administrator of Hejian for refusing to court his superiors, and the literati set never forgave him for it.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏名臣奏》載侍中辛毗奏曰：「昔桓階為尚書令，以崔林非尚書才，遷以為河間太守。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei mingchen zou records Attendant-in-Ordinary Xin Pi's memorial: "Formerly Huan Jie was Master of Writing and, because Cui Lin was not Master of Writing material, transferred him to be Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Memorials of Wei Notables preserves Xin Pi's protest: when Huan Jie headed the Masters of Writing, he judged Cui Lin unsuited to that bureau and shifted him to Hejian instead.

sentences.zh: 」與此傳不同。〉

translations.literal: 〉"This differs from this biography.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〉"—a version that disagrees with the account given here.〉

sentences.zh: 遷大鴻臚。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 龜茲王遣侍子來朝，朝廷嘉其遠至，襃賞其王甚厚。

translations.literal: The king of Qiuci sent a hostage son to court; the court praised his having come from afar, and richly rewarded and enfeoffed his king.
translations.idiomatic: When the king of Kucha sent a princely hostage to Luoyang, the court lavished titles and gifts on the distant ruler.

sentences.zh: 餘國各遣子來朝，閒使連屬，林恐所遣或非真的，權取疏屬賈胡，因通使命，利得印綬，而道路護送，所損滋多。

translations.literal: The remaining states each sent sons to court; sporadic envoys followed one after another. Lin feared that those sent might not be genuine, and temporarily took distant collateral merchant Hu, and through them communicated missions, profiting to obtain seals and cords, while on the roads escorting and guarding, what was lost became ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Other kingdoms began sending their own "sons" in an endless stream of envoys. Cui Lin worried that many were impostors—distant cousins or Sogdian traders buying patents of investiture—while the cost of escorts along the highway kept mounting.

sentences.zh: 勞所養之民，資無益之事，為夷狄所笑，此曩時之所患也。

translations.literal: Toiling the people whom we nurture, supplying a useless undertaking, and being laughed at by the Yi and Di—this was what was worried about in former times.
translations.idiomatic: It wastes the people we are meant to protect, funds a pointless pageant, and invites ridicule from the border peoples—the very abuse earlier dynasties deplored.

sentences.zh: 乃移書燉煌喻指，并錄前世待遇諸國豐約故事，使有恒常。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent a dispatch to Dunhuang explaining the intent, and also recorded the precedents of former generations' treatment of the various states, abundant or meager, so that there would be constancy.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote Dunhuang spelling out court policy and attached a digest of how past regimes had treated foreign princes, thick or thin, so that practice would settle into a steady rule.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，賜爵關內侯，轉光祿勳、司隷校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he was granted the rank of marquis within the passes, and transferred to Supervisor of the Household for the Imperial Clan and Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Rui came to the throne, Cui Lin received a secondary marquisate, then moved to supervisor of the imperial clan bureau and colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 屬郡皆罷非法除過員吏。

translations.literal: The subordinate commanderies all abolished illegally appointed excess clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every county under his jurisdiction to purge supernumerary appointees made without proper warrant.

sentences.zh: 林為政推誠，簡存大體，是以去後每輒見思。

translations.literal: Lin's governance pushed sincerity and selected what preserved the great pattern; therefore after he left, each time he was remembered with longing.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin governed with candor and kept his eye on essentials, so that wherever he served, people missed him after he left.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍劉劭作考課論，制下百僚。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Shao composed a treatise on merit evaluation, and regulations were issued to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao, as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, drafted a blueprint for grading officials, and the throne circulated it to the whole bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 林議曰：「案周官考課，其文備矣，自康王以下，遂以陵遲，此即考課之法存乎其人也。

translations.literal: Lin debated, saying: "According to the Zhou offices' merit evaluation, the text is complete; from King Kang downward, it thereupon declined—this is a case where the method of merit evaluation existed in the men who applied it.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin argued: "The Rites of Zhou already spell out inspection of merit; after King Kang the system decayed—proof that written rules matter less than the integrity of the men who wield them.

sentences.zh: 及漢之季，其失豈在乎佐吏之職不密哉？

translations.literal: Reaching the end of Han, was its failure really in the clerks' duties not being tight?"
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Han collapsed, was the flaw really that aides kept sloppy files?"

sentences.zh: 方今軍旅，或猥或卒，備之以科條，申之以內外，增減無常，固難一矣。

translations.literal: At present for military affairs, sometimes they are numerous, sometimes sudden; preparing them with statutes and ordinances, extending them internally and externally, increase and decrease are not constant—solidly it is hard to unify.
translations.idiomatic: Today armies march at a moment's notice or swell without warning; statutes multiply, inner and outer bureaus tug the rules in opposite directions—no single ledger can cover every case.

sentences.zh: 且萬目不張舉其綱，衆毛不整振其領。

translations.literal: Moreover when the myriad eyes do not open, raise the net rope; when the many hairs are not ordered, shake the collar.
translations.idiomatic: As the adage says, lift the main cord when the mesh will not spread; straighten the collar when the fur lies awry.

sentences.zh: 臯陶仕虞，伊尹臣殷，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Gao Yao served Yu; Yi Yin was minister to Yin; the unkindly stayed far away.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yao served Shun, Yi Yin served the Yin kings, and the vicious simply melted away.

sentences.zh: 五帝三王未必如一，而各以治亂。

translations.literal: The Five Thearchs and Three Kings were not necessarily identical, yet each thereby brought order or chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Thearchs and Three Kings never ruled alike, yet each age found its own path to order or ruin.

sentences.zh: 易曰：『易簡，而天下之理得矣。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'Easy and simple, and the patterns of All under Heaven are obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou yi teaches: "Keep policy plain and easy, and the way of the world becomes clear."

sentences.zh: 』太祖隨宜設辟，以遺來今，不患不法古也。

translations.literal: 'The Grand Progenitor as occasion suited established recruitment, to bequeath to later times; one need not worry about not modeling antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder tailored recruitment to circumstance and left us that flexibility; we need not obsess over copying antiquity."

sentences.zh: 以為今之制度，不為疏闊，惟在守一勿失而已。

translations.literal: He considered that today's institutions are not lax; the only thing is in guarding unity and not losing it.
translations.idiomatic: Our present institutions are not too loose; the task is simply to hold the line without drifting.

sentences.zh: 若朝臣能任仲山甫之重，式是百辟，則孰敢不肅？」

translations.literal: If court ministers could bear the weight of Zhong Shanfu, and thereby model the hundred sheiks, then who would dare not be reverent?"
translations.idiomatic: Give us ministers with the backbone of Zhong Shanfu to awe the regional heads, and who would dare slacken?"

sentences.zh: 魯相上言：「漢舊立孔子廟，襃成侯歲時奉祠，辟雍行禮，必祭先師，王家出穀，春秋祭祀。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of Lu submitted a memorial saying: "According to Han precedent a temple to Confucius was established; the marquis who continues his praise offered seasonal sacrifices, and at the Biyong when performing rites they invariably sacrificed to the first teacher; the royal house issued grain, and spring and autumn sacrifices were performed.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of Lu memorialized: "Han law maintained a Confucian shrine; the marquis who "continues the praise" tended its seasonal rites; the circular moat academy always honored the First Teacher; the imperial clan supplied grain for spring and autumn offerings.

sentences.zh: 今宗聖侯奉嗣，未有命祭之禮，宜給牲牢，長吏奉祀，尊為貴神。

translations.literal: Now the marquis who continues the sage receives the succession, but there is not the ritual of mandated sacrifice; it is fitting to supply victims and grain, the senior officials perform sacrifice, and honor him as a lofty spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Today the marquis who "continues the sage" lacks a statutory cult; he should receive oxen and grain, with local magistrates conducting the service and the sage ranked among the highest gods."

sentences.zh: 」制三府議，博士傅祗以春秋傳言立在祀典，則孔子是也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Offices to debate; Erudite Fu Di, citing the Zuo zhuan's statement that those established in the sacrificial canon include Confucius, was of this view.
translations.idiomatic: The throne told the Three Dukes to debate the point. Erudite Fu Di cited the Zuo Tradition: whoever is entered in the state register of sacrifices deserves worship—Confucius plainly qualifies.

sentences.zh: 宗聖適足繼絕世，章盛德耳。

translations.literal: The marquis who continues the sage merely suffices to continue a severed line, and display abundant virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The "sage's heir" title only keeps an extinct line alive and advertises imperial largesse.

sentences.zh: 至於顯立言，崇明德，則宜如魯相所上。

translations.literal: As for displaying established teachings and exalting bright virtue, then it is fitting as the Chancellor of Lu submitted.
translations.idiomatic: If the goal is to broadcast the Master's doctrine and honor his virtue, the Lu memorial has the right of it.

sentences.zh: 林議以為「宗聖侯亦以王命祀，不為未有命也。

translations.literal: Lin debated, considering that "the marquis who continues the sage also by royal mandate sacrifices; it is not that there is no mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin countered that the marquis already sacrificed by imperial writ—hardly an "unmandated" cult.

sentences.zh: 周武王封黃帝、堯、舜之後，及立三恪，禹、湯之世，不列于時，復特命他官祭也。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed the descendants of the Yellow Thearch, Yao, and Shun, and moreover established the three guest houses; in the eras of Yu and Tang they were not listed in their time, and again he specially ordered other officials to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu enfeoffed the Yellow Thearch's line and those of Yao and Shun and added the "three reverend houses," yet in Yu's or Tang's day they were not on the regular roster—other officers handled their offerings.

sentences.zh: 今周公已上，達於三皇，忽焉不祀，而其禮經亦存其言。

translations.literal: Now from the Duke of Zhou upward, reaching to the Three August Ones, suddenly they are not sacrificed to, yet their ritual classics also preserve their words.
translations.idiomatic: From the Duke of Zhou back to the Three August Ones the classics still name them, yet we no longer maintain their altars.

sentences.zh: 今獨祀孔子者，以世近故也。

translations.literal: Now the sole one sacrificed to is Confucius, because the generations are near.
translations.idiomatic: We single out Confucius chiefly because his age lies closest to our own.

sentences.zh: 以大夫之後，特受無疆之祀，禮過古帝，義踰湯、武，可謂崇明報德矣，無復重祀於非族也。」

translations.literal: As a great officer's descendant, he specially receives boundless sacrifice; ritual surpasses the ancient thearchs, meaning exceeds Tang and Wu—this may be called exalting the bright and repaying virtue; there is no need again to double sacrifices to unrelated clans."
translations.idiomatic: To give a minister's heir limitless oblations—outranking ancient thearchs and outshining even Tang and Wu—is already the utmost "exalting virtue"; we need not pile duplicate rites on unrelated forebears."

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為孟軻稱宰我之辭曰：「予以觀夫子，賢於堯舜遠矣。

translations.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi considers: Meng Ke cited Zai Wo's words, saying: "I look upon the Master—he is far worthier than Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi comments: Mencius quoted Zai Wo—"Compared with the Master, even Yao and Shun seem lesser men."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「生民以來，未有盛於孔子者也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since life was given to the people, none has been greater than Confucius."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "In all the lives Heaven has granted humankind, none matches Confucius."

sentences.zh: 」斯非通賢之格言，商較之定準乎！

translations.literal: Are these not the maxims of thorough worthies, the fixed standard for weighing excellence!
translations.idiomatic: Are those not the very yardstick by which the wise judge greatness!

sentences.zh: 雖妙極則同，萬聖猶一，然淳薄異時，質文殊用，或當時則榮，沒則已焉，是以遺風所被，寔有深淺。

translations.literal: Although the subtle utmost is the same and the myriad sages are still one, yet purity and thinness differ in age, substance and pattern differ in use, or at the time they were glorious, when gone they were finished; therefore where the legacy wind spreads, truly there is depth and shallowness.
translations.idiomatic: Ultimate truth may be one, yet ages differ in simplicity or decadence, and genius takes many forms—some blaze only in their own day. That is why later reverence runs deep for some teachers and shallow for others.

sentences.zh: 若乃經緯天人，立言垂制，百王莫之能違，彝倫資之以立，誠一人而已耳。

translations.literal: As for ordering Heaven and man, establishing teachings and handing down models, the hundred kings none could transgress, and constant human relations rely on them to stand—indeed there is one person only.
translations.idiomatic: To weave Heaven and humanity into one teaching, to set a model every throne must acknowledge—there stands truly only one such man.

sentences.zh: 周監二代，斯文為盛。

translations.literal: Zhou surveyed the two dynasties; this culture was most flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou house looked back on Xia and Shang; its ritual culture reached a peak.

sentences.zh: 然於六經之道，未能及其精致。

translations.literal: Yet on the way of the Six Classics, it was unable to reach their refined utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Zhou learning never quite matched the subtlety of the Six Classics themselves.

sentences.zh: 加以聖賢不興，曠年五百，道化陵夷，憲章殆滅，若使時無孔門，則周典幾乎息矣。

translations.literal: Add that sage and worthy did not arise, blank years were five hundred, the transforming Way declined and fell, statutes and patterns nearly perished; if at the time there had been no Kong school, then Zhou canons would almost have ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred years without a sage left the moral order in tatters; had Confucius and his disciples not rescued the texts, Zhou civilization might have died on the vine.

sentences.zh: 夫能光明先王之道，以成萬世之功，齊天地之無窮，等日月之久照，豈不有踰於羣聖哉？

translations.literal: As for one who could brighten the way of the former kings, thereby completing merit for myriad generations, equal to Heaven and earth's boundlessness, matching sun and moon's long shining—how could he not surpass the crowd of sages?
translations.idiomatic: How could a teacher who relit the ancient kings' path, secured merit for endless generations, and rivals heaven and earth in endurance be anything less than greater than every other so-called sage?

sentences.zh: 林曾無史遷洞想之誠，梅真慷慨之志，而守其蓬心以塞明義，可謂多見其不知量也。〉

translations.literal: Lin never had Sima Qian's sincerity of penetrating reflection, or Mei Fu's generous ardor, yet guarded his thistle heart to block clear meaning—this can be called much seeing his not knowing measure.〉
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin showed neither Sima Qian's luminous empathy nor Mei Fu's indignant zeal—only a pedant's stubbornness masquerading as principle. He simply did not know his own measure.〉

sentences.zh: 高柔字文惠，陳留圉人也。

translations.literal: Gao Rou, courtesy name Wenhui, was a man of Yu in Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou, courtesy name Wenhui, came from Yu in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父靖，為蜀郡都尉。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Commandant of Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao Jing had served as commandant of Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《陳留耆舊傳》曰：靖高祖父固，不仕王莽世，為淮陽太守所害，以烈節垂名。

translations.literal: 〈The Chenliu qijiu zhuan says: Jing's high grandfather Gu, not serving in Wang Mang's age, was harmed by the Administrator of Huaiyang, and by fierce integrity transmitted his name.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Chenliu Traditions of the Elderly states that Gao Jing's great-great-grandfather Gao Gu refused office under Wang Mang and was murdered by the Administrator of Huaiyang, winning posthumous fame for his steadfast honor.

sentences.zh: 固子慎，字孝甫。

translations.literal: Gu's son Shen, courtesy name Xiaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's son Gao Shen bore the courtesy name Xiaofu.

sentences.zh: 敦厚少華，有沈深之量。

translations.literal: Thick and honest, little ornament, he had the capacity of deep stillness.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain, steady, and unflashy, with a calm depth about him.

sentences.zh: 撫育孤兄子五人，恩義甚篤。

translations.literal: He raised and nurtured five orphan sons of his elder brother, and grace and righteousness were very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his late brother's five sons as his own, with unstinting kindness.

sentences.zh: 琅邪相何英嘉其行履，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of Langye, He Ying, praised his conduct and practice, and with his daughter married him.
translations.idiomatic: He Ying, chancellor of Langye, admired his character and gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 英即車騎將軍熈之父也。

translations.literal: Ying was the father of General of Chariots and Cavalry Xi.
translations.idiomatic: That He Ying was the father of General of Chariots and Cavalry He Xi.

sentences.zh: 慎歷二縣令、東萊太守。

translations.literal: Shen passed through two county magistracies and Administrator of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shen served as magistrate of two counties and then as administrator of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 老病歸家，草屋蓬戶，甕缶無儲。

translations.literal: Old and ill he returned home, grass hut and thistle door, jars and pots without stores.
translations.idiomatic: Age and illness drove him home to a thatched hovel with not a jar of grain in reserve.

sentences.zh: 其妻謂之曰：「君累經宰守，積有年歲，何能不少為儲畜以遺子孫乎？

translations.literal: His wife said to him: "You have repeatedly passed through magistrate and guard posts, accumulated years—how can you not a little store up to bequeath to sons and grandsons?"
translations.idiomatic: His wife asked, "You have been magistrate and two-thousand-bushel official year after year—could you not salt away something for the children?"

sentences.zh: 」慎曰：「我以勤身清名為之基，以二千石遺之，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Shen said: "I take diligent body and pure name as their foundation, and with two thousand shi bequeath to them—is it not acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shen answered, "I leave them an honest name earned by toil and a father who held a two-thousand-bushel post—is that not inheritance enough!"

sentences.zh: 」子式，至孝，常盡力供養。

translations.literal: His son Shi, supremely filial, constantly exhausted his strength to supply nurture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Shi was famously filial and strained every nerve to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 永初中，螟蝗為害，獨不食式麥，圉令周彊以表州郡。

translations.literal: In the Yongchu era, moths and locusts did harm; alone they did not eat Shi's wheat; the magistrate of Yu, Zhou Qiang, memorialized this to the province and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongchu locust plague, the swarms devoured every field except Gao Shi's; Magistrate Zhou Qiang of Yu reported the miracle to his superiors.

sentences.zh: 太守楊舜舉式孝子，讓不行。

translations.literal: Administrator Yang Shun recommended Shi as filial son; he declined and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Yang Shun nominated him as an exemplar of filial piety, but Gao Shi modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 後以孝廉為郎。

translations.literal: Later by filial and incorrupt he became a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered office as a gentleman cadet on a filial-and-incorrupt recommendation.

sentences.zh: 次子昌，昌弟賜，並為刺史、郡守。

translations.literal: The second son Chang, and Chang's younger brother Ci, both were inspectors and administrators.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Gao Chang and younger son Gao Ci both rose to inspector and grand administrator posts.

sentences.zh: 式子弘，孝廉。

translations.literal: Shi's son Hong was filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi's son Gao Hong also earned a filial-and-incorrupt nomination.

sentences.zh: 弘生靖。〉

translations.literal: Hong begat Jing.〉
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hong was the father of Gao Jing.〉

sentences.zh: 柔留鄉里，謂邑中曰：「今者英雄並起，陳留四戰之地也。

translations.literal: Rou remained in his home village, saying to the district: "At present heroes rise together; Chenliu is a land fought over from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou stayed in his home county and warned his neighbors, "Warlords are rising on every side, and Chenliu lies at the crossroads of four armies.

sentences.zh: 曹將軍雖據兖州，本有四方之圖，未得安坐守也。

translations.literal: Although General Cao occupies Yan Province, originally he has plans on the four quarters, and cannot obtain sitting guard in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao may hold Yan Province, but his ambitions range beyond it—he will not sit idle.

sentences.zh: 而張府君先得志於陳留，吾恐變乘間作也，欲與諸君避之。

translations.literal: Yet Prefect Zhang has first obtained his will in Chenliu; I fear change will take advantage of intervals to arise; I wish with you gentlemen to avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao already controls Chenliu; I fear trouble will break out between them—I urge everyone to leave while we can."

sentences.zh: 」衆人皆以張邈與太祖善，柔又年少，不然其言。

translations.literal: The crowd all considered that Zhang Miao and the Grand Progenitor were friendly, and Rou was moreover young, and did not consider his words correct.
translations.idiomatic: They only scoffed: Zhang Miao was Cao Cao's old friend, and Gao Rou was too young to know anything.

sentences.zh: 柔從兄幹，袁紹甥也，

translations.literal: Rou's elder cousin Gan was Yuan Shao's nephew,
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou was tied by kinship to Gao Gan, who was Yuan Shao's nephew.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承《後漢書》曰：幹字元才。

translations.literal: 〈Xie Cheng's Hou Han shu says: Gan's courtesy name was Yuancai.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xie Cheng's Later Han History gives Gao Gan the courtesy name Yuancai.

sentences.zh: 才志弘邈，文武秀出。

translations.literal: His talents and purpose were vast and distant; civil and military stood out.
translations.idiomatic: He combined wide vision with real ability in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 父躬，蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Gong was Administrator of Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao Gong had governed Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖賜，司隷校尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ci was Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gao Ci had been colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 案陳留耆舊傳及謝承書，幹應為柔從父，非從兄也。

translations.literal: According to the Chenliu qijiu zhuan and Xie Cheng's book, Gan ought to be Rou's uncle's son, not elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenliu elder traditions and Xie Cheng's history both make Gao Gan Gao Rou's first cousin once removed, not an elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 未知何者為誤。〉

translations.literal: It is not known which is erroneous.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi cannot tell which genealogy is wrong.〉

sentences.zh: 在河北呼柔，柔舉宗從之。

translations.literal: In Hebei he called Rou; Rou raised the lineage and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gan summoned him to the north, Gao Rou moved the whole clan to join him.

sentences.zh: 會靖卒於西州，時道路艱澁，兵寇縱橫，而柔冒艱險詣蜀迎喪，辛苦荼毒，無所不嘗，三年乃還。

translations.literal: It happened that Jing died in the western province; at that time roads were hard and obstructed, soldiers and bandits ran rampant, yet Rou braved hardship and danger to go to Shu to welcome the coffin, bitterly toiling in extreme poison, nothing he did not taste; only after three years did he return.
translations.idiomatic: Then word came that Gao Jing had died in the west; roads were cut by warlords and bandits, yet Gao Rou fought his way to Shu, spent three years escorting his father's bier home through every hardship imaginable.

sentences.zh: 太祖平袁氏，以柔為菅長。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified the Yuan clan, he appointed Rou as Magistrate of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao crushed the Yuans, he named Gao Rou magistrate of Jian county.

sentences.zh: 縣中素聞其名，姧吏數人皆自引去。

translations.literal: In the county they long had heard his name; several corrupt clerks all on their own withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The county clerks had heard his reputation; several corrupt men resigned before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 柔教曰：「昔邴吉臨政，吏嘗有非，猶尚容之。

translations.literal: Rou instructed, saying: "Formerly Bing Ji presided over government; clerks once had faults, yet still tolerated them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou announced, "When Bing Ji governed, he forgave minor faults in his staff.

sentences.zh: 況此諸吏，於吾未有失乎！

translations.literal: How much more these various clerks—for me they have had no failures!"
translations.idiomatic: These men have done nothing wrong by me!"

sentences.zh: 其召復之。

translations.literal: Order them summoned back."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them recalled to their posts."

sentences.zh: 」咸還，皆自勵，咸為佳吏。

translations.literal: All returned; all on their own urged themselves, and all became fine clerks.
translations.idiomatic: They returned, ashamed and determined, and became a model staff.

sentences.zh: 高幹旣降，頃之以并州叛。

translations.literal: After Gao Gan had surrendered, in a short while he rebelled with Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after surrendering, Gao Gan rose in revolt with Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 柔自歸太祖，太祖欲因事誅之，以為刺姧令史；

translations.literal: Rou on his own returned to the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor wished to use the affair to execute him, and appointed him clerk for arresting malfeasance;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou slipped back to Cao Cao, who briefly thought of executing him for kinship with the rebel, then instead named him clerk for criminal investigation;

sentences.zh: 處法允當，獄無留滯，辟為丞相倉曹屬。

translations.literal: his handling of law was fair and appropriate, prisons had no backlog, and he was summoned as an aide in the Chancellor's granary bureau.
translations.idiomatic: he judged cases with scrupulous fairness, cleared the jails, and was promoted to the Chancellor's granary office.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：柔旣處法平允，又夙夜匪懈，至擁膝抱文書而寢。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei shi chunqiu says: Rou, having handled law fairly and evenly, moreover from dawn to night without slackening, reached hugging his knees and embracing documents while sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Spring and Autumn Annals of the House of Wei notes that Gao Rou worked such long fair shifts that he fell asleep hugging case files.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗夜微出，觀察諸吏，見柔，哀之，徐解裘覆柔而去。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once at night secretly went out to observe the various clerks; seeing Rou, pitied him, slowly removed his fur robe to cover Rou and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao once made a midnight inspection of his offices, found Gao Rou asleep at his desk, pitied him, and draped his own fur cloak over him before leaving.

sentences.zh: 自是辟焉。〉

translations.literal: From this he was summoned.〉
translations.idiomatic: After that incident Cao Cao formally promoted him.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖欲遣鍾繇等討張魯，柔諫，以為今猥遣大兵，西有韓遂、馬超，謂為己舉，將相扇動作逆，宜先招集三輔，三輔苟平，漢中可傳檄而定也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor wished to dispatch Zhong Yao and others to campaign against Zhang Lu; Rou remonstrated, considering that now rashly dispatching a great army, west having Han Sui and Ma Chao, they would consider it raised against themselves, generals and ministers would fan each other into rebellion; it was fitting first to summon and gather the Three Adjuncts; if the Three Adjuncts were roughly pacified, Hanzhong could be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao planned to send Zhong Yao west against Zhang Lu, Gao Rou objected: a massive expedition would panic Han Sui and Ma Chao into thinking they were the target and invite mutiny; secure the Guanzhong heartland first, he urged, and Hanzhong would fall to a summons.

sentences.zh: 繇入關，遂、超等果反。

translations.literal: When Yao entered the passes, Sui, Chao and others indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao crossed the passes as ordered; Han Sui and Ma Chao promptly rebelled.

sentences.zh: 魏國初建，為尚書郎。

translations.literal: When the state of Wei was first established, he became a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the kingdom of Wei was founded he entered the Masters of Writing as a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 轉拜丞相理曹掾，令曰：「夫治定之化，以禮為首。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed aide in the Chancellor's bureau of law, an order saying: "As for the transforming influence of settled rule, ritual comes first.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to the Chancellor's law bureau with an edict reading, "In peacetime, teach with ritual first.

sentences.zh: 撥亂之政，以刑為先。

translations.literal: As for the government that pulls up chaos, punishment comes first.
translations.idiomatic: In times of chaos, begin with punishment.

sentences.zh: 是以舜流四凶族，臯陶作士。

translations.literal: Therefore Shun banished the four evil clans, and Gao Yao was made minister of crime.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Shun exiled the Four Fiends and made Gao Yao minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 漢祖除秦苛法，蕭何定律。

translations.literal: Han's progenitor removed Qin's harsh laws, and Xiao He fixed the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder swept away Qin's cruel code; Xiao He rebuilt the statutes.

sentences.zh: 掾清識平當，明于憲典，勉恤之哉！

translations.literal: Aide, your discernment is pure, your judgments even, you are clear on statutes and canons—strive to be compassionate in them!"
translations.idiomatic: You are clear-sighted, even-handed, and master the code—apply it with mercy!"

sentences.zh: 」鼓吹宋金等在合肥亡逃。

translations.literal: The musicians Song Jin and others at Hefei fled.
translations.idiomatic: The military musicians Song Jin and their mates deserted at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 舊法，軍征士亡，考竟其妻子。

translations.literal: By old statute, when soldiers on campaign deserted, their wives and children were investigated to the end (executed).
translations.idiomatic: Under the old code, a deserter's wife and children could be put to death after inquiry.

sentences.zh: 太祖患猶不息，更重其刑。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor worried it still did not cease, and further increased the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao found the practice still failed to stop desertion and made the penalty harsher still.

sentences.zh: 金有母妻及二弟皆給官，主者奏盡殺之。

translations.literal: Jin had a mother, wife, and two younger brothers all assigned to government service; the presiding official memorialized to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jin's mother, wife, and two brothers were all held as government dependents; the clerk in charge asked permission to execute the entire family.

sentences.zh: 柔啟曰：「士卒亡軍，誠在可疾，然竊聞其中時有悔者。

translations.literal: Rou presented a memorial saying: "Soldiers who desert the army are indeed to be detested; yet your subject has privately heard that among them there are sometimes those who repent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou replied: "Deserters deserve contempt, yet some later repent.

sentences.zh: 愚謂乃宜貸其妻子，一可使賊中不信，二可使誘其還心。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject considers that one ought to spare their wives and children: first, it can make those in the enemy ranks not trust each other; second, it can entice their hearts to return.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to spare their families: the enemy will trust one another less, and wavering men will have a reason to come back.

sentences.zh: 正如前科，固已絕其意望，而猥復重之，柔恐自今在軍之士，見一人亡逃，誅將及己，亦且相隨而走，不可復得殺也。

translations.literal: Just as under the former statute, solidly their hope and expectation were already cut off, yet vulgarly again increasing it, Rou fears that from now on soldiers in the army, seeing one man desert and execution reaching themselves, will also thereupon flee one after another, and cannot again be killed off.
translations.idiomatic: The old law already left deserters hopeless; to heap worse punishment on their kin will only convince every soldier in the ranks that when one man runs, his comrades die too—so they will bolt in chains and you will never catch them all.

sentences.zh: 此重刑非所以止亡，乃所以益走耳。

translations.literal: This heavy punishment is not the means to stop desertion; it is the means to increase flight.
translations.idiomatic: Such cruelty does not stop desertion; it multiplies it.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: 〉The Grand Progenitor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: 〉Cao Cao said, "Well argued."

sentences.zh: 」即止不殺金母、弟，蒙活者甚衆。

translations.literal: 〉Thereupon he immediately did not kill Jin's mother and younger brothers; those who received life were very many.
translations.idiomatic: 〉He stayed the execution of Jin's mother and brothers, and a great many others owed their lives to the decision.

sentences.zh: 遷為潁川太守，復還為法曹掾。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Administrator of Yingchuan, and again returned to be aide in the law bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou was promoted to Administrator of Yingchuan, then recalled to serve again as law-bureau aide.

sentences.zh: 時置校事盧洪、趙達等，使察羣下，柔諫曰：「設官分職，各有所司。

translations.literal: At that time were appointed surveillance officials Lu Hong, Zhao Da, and others, to make them investigate the officials below; Rou remonstrated, saying: "Establishing offices and dividing duties, each has what he manages.
translations.idiomatic: When the court named Lu Hong, Zhao Da, and other "surveillance" agents to spy on the bureaucracy, Gao Rou protested: "Government works by fixed offices and clear portfolios.

sentences.zh: 今置校事，旣非居上信下之旨。

translations.literal: Now appointing surveillance officials is already not the intent of those above trusting those below.
translations.idiomatic: These roving inquisitors are the opposite of trusting ministers with their jobs.

sentences.zh: 又達等數以憎愛擅作威福，宜檢治之。

translations.literal: Moreover Da and others repeatedly by love and hate arbitrarily wielded favor and awe; it is fitting to investigate and punish them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Da and his like have repeatedly thrown their weight around from private likes and dislikes—they should be investigated and punished."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「卿知達等，恐不如吾也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "You know Da and others—perhaps you are not as good as I am.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, "You may think you know Zhao Da; I know him better.

sentences.zh: 要能刺舉而辨衆事，使賢人君子為之，則不能也。

translations.literal: What is needed is to be able to expose and report and distinguish the myriad affairs; if worthy men and gentlemen did it, they could not."
translations.idiomatic: The job takes informers who can sift every rumor—no gentleman could stomach it."

sentences.zh: 昔叔孫通用羣盜，良有以也。

translations.literal: Formerly Shu Sun Tong used a crowd of bandits—there truly was reason for it."
translations.idiomatic: Shu Sun Tong once staffed his rites with bandits for good reason."

sentences.zh: 」達等後姧利發，太祖殺之以謝於柔。

translations.literal: 〉Later Da and others' wicked profiteering came to light; the Grand Progenitor killed them to apologize to Rou.
translations.idiomatic: 〉When Zhao Da's corruption surfaced, Cao Cao executed him and his confederates and made a point of apologizing to Gao Rou.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，以柔為治書侍御史，賜爵關內侯，轉加治書執法。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he appointed Rou as Palace Assistant Secretary for Documents, granted the rank of marquis within the passes, and transferred him to add the title Assistant for Documents and Law Enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne he named Gao Rou palace assistant secretary for documents, enfeoffed him as a secondary marquis, and added the post of assistant for documents and law enforcement.

sentences.zh: 民間數有誹謗妖言，帝疾之，有妖言輒殺，而賞告者。

translations.literal: Among the people there were repeatedly slanderous and occult words; the Emperor hated it; whenever there were occult words he immediately killed, and rewarded those who reported.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderous "prophetic" talk spread in the countryside; Cao Pi detested it, executed every accused author, and paid informers.

sentences.zh: 柔上疏曰：「今妖言者必戮，告之者輒賞。

translations.literal: Rou submitted a memorial saying: "Now those who speak occult words are invariably executed, and those who report them are invariably rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou wrote: "You kill every rumor-monger and reward every accuser.

sentences.zh: 旣使過誤無反善之路，又將開凶狡之羣相誣罔之漸，誠非所以息姧省訟，緝熈治道也。

translations.literal: This both makes those who err have no road to return to goodness, and moreover will open the step of wicked and crafty crowds mutually slandering falsely—truly this is not the means to still wickedness and reduce lawsuits, to gather brightness and order the Way."
translations.idiomatic: That leaves the misguided no path to reform, and invites vicious men to frame one another—hardly the way to reduce lawsuits or brighten the realm."

sentences.zh: 昔周公作誥，稱殷之祖宗，咸不顧小人之怨。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou made the announcements, praising Yin's ancestors, all not caring about petty men's resentments.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou's proclamations praised Yin's forebears and brushed aside small men's grudges.

sentences.zh: 在漢太宗，亦除妖言誹謗之令。

translations.literal: In Han's Emperor Wen, he also abolished the statutes on occult words and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han repealed the laws against "prophecy" and defamation.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜除妖謗賞告之法，以隆天父養物之仁。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject considers it fitting to abolish the law on occult slander and rewarding informers, thereby to elevate Heaven the Father's benevolence in nurturing things."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to repeal the witch-hunt rewards and show the compassion of Heaven toward its creatures."

sentences.zh: 」帝不即從，而相誣告者滋甚。

translations.literal: 〉The Emperor did not immediately follow, yet those who mutually falsely accused became ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: 〉The emperor hesitated, and malicious denunciations multiplied.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔：「敢以誹謗相告者，以所告者罪罪之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict: "Whoever dares to accuse another of slander, let him suffer the punishment of the one accused."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi then decreed: "Whoever lodges a slander charge will himself suffer the penalty he sought for his victim."

sentences.zh: 」於是遂絕。

translations.literal: 〉Thereupon it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: 〉The flood of false accusations dried up.

sentences.zh: 校事劉慈等，自黃初初數年之閒，舉吏民姧罪以萬數，柔皆請懲虛實；

translations.literal: The surveillance official Liu Ci and others, from the beginning of Huangchu across several years, reported officials and commoners' wicked crimes numbering in the tens of thousands; Rou all requested to verify truth and falsity;
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years of Huangchu, surveillance agent Liu Ci and his colleagues denounced tens of thousands of supposed crimes; Gao Rou insisted each case be checked for substance;

sentences.zh: 其餘小小挂法者，不過罰金。

translations.literal: the rest who slightly brushed the law, he did not exceed fining in cash.
translations.idiomatic: petty offenders he punished with fines at most.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷為廷尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to be Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangchu he became commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 魏初，三公無事，又希與朝政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, the Three Dukes had no affairs, and moreover rarely participated in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wei dynasty the three dukes had little real work and seldom joined policy debates.

sentences.zh: 柔上疏曰：「天地以四時成功，元首以輔弼興治；

translations.literal: Rou submitted a memorial saying: "Heaven and earth by the four seasons complete their work; the sovereign's head by assistants and supports raises order;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou wrote: "Heaven finishes its year through the seasons; a ruler finishes his task through good ministers;

sentences.zh: 成湯杖阿衡之佐，文、武憑旦、望之力，逮至漢初，蕭、曹之儔並以元勳代作心膂，此皆明王聖主任臣於上，賢相良輔股肱於下也。

translations.literal: Cheng Tang leaned on the help of Ah Heng, Wen and Wu relied on the strength of Dan and Wang; reaching to Han's beginning, Xiao and Cao's sort together by first merit substituted as heart and liver—this is all enlightened kings and sage lords entrusting ministers above, worthy chancellors and fine assistants being arms and thighs below."
translations.idiomatic: Tang leaned on Yi Yin; the Zhou kings on the Duke of Zhou and Jiang Taigong; at Han's founding Xiao He and Cao Shen turned battlefield merit into the emperor's right hand—true partnership between throne and ministers."

sentences.zh: 今公輔之臣，皆國之棟梁，民所具瞻，而置之三事，不使知政，遂各偃息養高，鮮有進納，誠非朝廷崇用大臣之義，大臣獻可替否之謂也。

translations.literal: Now the ducal ministers are all the state's pillars and beams, what the people all gaze upon, yet placing them in the Three Affairs, not letting them know government, thereupon each rests and nourishes lofty reclusion, rarely having advance and presentation—truly this is not the court's meaning of honoring and employing great ministers, nor what great ministers mean by presenting the feasible and replacing the unfeasible."
translations.idiomatic: Your dukes are the empire's roof timbers and the people's mirror, yet you park them in empty honor, bar them from policy, and let them idle away their prestige—hardly the way to "honor great ministers," nor how ministers "approve the sound and reject the unsound."

sentences.zh: 古者刑政有疑，輒議於槐棘之下。

translations.literal: In antiquity when punishments and government had doubts, they always debated beneath the locust and thorn trees.
translations.idiomatic: When ancient kings doubted a case, they opened debate under the court's "locust and zelkova"—the place for public justice.

sentences.zh: 自今之後，朝有疑議及刑獄大事，宜數以咨訪三公。

translations.literal: From now afterward, when the court has doubtful deliberations and great matters of punishments and prisons, it is fitting frequently thereby to consult and visit the Three Dukes."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every doubtful policy or major criminal case should be referred to the three dukes for counsel."

sentences.zh: 三公朝朔望之日，又可特延入，講論得失，博盡事情，庶有裨起天聽，弘益大化。

translations.literal: On the days when the Three Dukes attend court at the new and full moons, one may also specially extend them entry, lecture and discuss gain and loss, broadly exhaust the circumstances of affairs, perhaps thereby to benefit and rouse Heaven's hearing, and enlarge and benefit the great transformation."
translations.idiomatic: On the regular audience days you might also keep them after court to thrash out policy in detail—so your ears stay open and the realm profits."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: 〉The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: 〉The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝以宿嫌，欲枉法誅治書執法鮑勛，而柔固執不從詔命。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of old resentment, wished to bend the law to execute Assistant for Documents and Law Enforcement Bao Xun, yet Rou firmly held and did not follow the edict's command.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi nursed an old grudge against Bao Xun and tried to twist the statutes to have him killed; Gao Rou refused to sign the order.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，遂召柔詣臺；

translations.literal: The Emperor was extremely angry, thereupon summoned Rou to the terrace;
translations.idiomatic: Furious, the emperor summoned Gao Rou to the palace tower

sentences.zh: 遣使者承指至廷尉考竟勛，勛死乃遣柔還寺。

translations.literal: sent an envoy bearing his intent to the Commandant of Justice to investigate Xun to the end; when Xun died, then he sent Rou back to his office.
translations.idiomatic: and sent a runner to the commandant of justice with orders to torture Bao Xun to death; only after Xun died was Gao Rou allowed back to his yamen.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，封柔延壽亭侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Rou was enfeoffed as village marquis of Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Rui came to the throne he enfeoffed Gao Rou as village marquis of Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 時博士執經，柔上疏曰：「臣聞遵道重學，聖人洪訓；

translations.literal: At that time the erudites held the classics; Rou submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that honoring the Way and valuing learning is the sage's great instruction;
translations.idiomatic: While the court doctors lectured on the classics, Gao Rou wrote: "The sages teach us to revere learning.

sentences.zh: 褒文崇儒，帝者明義。

translations.literal: praising pattern and exalting Confucians is the enlightened ruler's clear duty.
translations.idiomatic: A wise sovereign promotes letters and respects scholars.

sentences.zh: 昔漢末陵遲，禮樂崩壞，雄戰虎爭，以戰陣為務，遂使儒林之羣，幽隱而不顯。

translations.literal: Formerly at Han's end it declined, ritual and music collapsed and broke, heroes warred like tigers, taking battle arrays as their task, thereupon causing the crowd of the Confucian forest to be hidden and not manifest.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han ritual collapsed and warlords fought like tigers; scholars were driven into obscurity.

sentences.zh: 太祖初興，愍其如此，在於撥亂之際，並使郡縣立教學之官。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first rose, he pitied it being thus; in the midst of pulling up chaos, he together ordered prefectures and counties to establish officials for teaching and learning.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder pitied them and, even while pacifying the realm, ordered every county to appoint education officers.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，遂闡其業，興復辟雍，州立課試，於是天下之士，復聞庠序之教，親俎豆之禮焉。

translations.literal: When the Exalted Ancestor ascended the throne, he thereupon expanded that enterprise, restored and raised the Biyong, established examinations at the provincial level, whereupon scholars of All under Heaven again heard the instruction of schools and personally witnessed the rites of the sacrificial stands and beans.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen (Cao Pi) succeeded, he expanded those schools, rebuilt the circular moat academy, and instituted provincial exams—so students once more heard lectures and watched the archery and banquet rites.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨政，允迪叡哲，敷弘大猷，光濟先軌，雖夏啟之承基，周成之繼業，誠無以加也。
