translations.literal: Your Majesty facing governance, truly treads sagely wisdom, spreads and magnifies the great plan, broadly aids the former tracks; although Xia Qi's inheriting the foundation, Zhou Cheng's continuing the enterprise, truly there is nothing to add.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules with sagely insight and carries forward their work; not even Qi of Xia or Cheng of Zhou has surpassed you.

sentences.zh: 然今博士皆經明行脩，一國清選，而使遷除限不過長，懼非所以崇顯儒術，帥勵怠惰也。

translations.literal: Yet now the erudites are all classics-bright and conduct cultivated, the state's pure selection, yet making promotions and transfers limited to not exceeding chief (zhang), Rou fears this is not the means to exalt and display Confucian arts, and lead and encourage the lazy."
translations.idiomatic: Yet your doctors are the pick of the empire—learned and upright—while promotion rules cap them at county chief rank; that hardly advertises Confucian learning or shames the idle."

sentences.zh: 孔子稱『舉善而教不能則勸』，故楚禮申公，學士銳精，漢隆卓茂，搢紳競慕。

translations.literal: Confucius called "raise the good and teach those who cannot, then they will be encouraged"; therefore Chu honored Duke Shen, and scholars sharpened their essence; Han elevated Zhuo Mao, and the gentry competed to admire.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Promote the worthy and coach the slow, and all strive": Chu honored Prince Shen and scholars burned midnight oil; Han exalted Zhuo Mao and gentlemen rushed to imitate.

sentences.zh: 臣以為博士者，道之淵藪，六藝所宗，宜隨學行優劣，待以不次之位。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that the erudites are the deep repository of the Way, what the Six Arts take as their ancestor; it is fitting according to learning and conduct's excellence or inferiority, to treat them with offices not in regular sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The doctors are the treasury of the Way and fountainhead of the Six Arts; rank them by merit and break the usual promotion ladder.

sentences.zh: 敦崇道教，以勸學者，於化為弘。

translations.literal: Earnestly exalt the Way's teaching, thereby to encourage learners—in transformation it is vast."
translations.idiomatic: Honor their vocation and students everywhere will take heart."

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: 〉The Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: 〉The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 後大興殿舍，百姓勞役；

translations.literal: Later he greatly raised palace halls and lodges, and the hundred surnames suffered corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Later the court launched vast palace projects that crushed the commoners with labor;

sentences.zh: 廣采衆女，充盈後宮；

translations.literal: broadly gathered crowds of women, filling the rear palace;
translations.idiomatic: drafted girls by the score until the harem overflowed;

sentences.zh: 後宮皇子連夭，繼嗣未育。

translations.literal: princes of the rear palace died in succession, and the heir had not yet been born.
translations.idiomatic: yet imperial sons died one after another and still no heir lived.

sentences.zh: 柔上疏曰：「二虜狡猾，潛自講肄，謀動干戈，未圖束手；

translations.literal: Rou submitted a memorial saying: "The two bandits are crafty, secretly on their own drilling and practicing, planning to move weapons and halberds, not yet thinking to bind their hands;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou warned: "Wu and Shu drill their armies in secret; they are not ready to surrender.

sentences.zh: 宜畜養將士，繕治甲兵，以逸待之。

translations.literal: it is fitting to nurture generals and soldiers, repair and complete armor and weapons, and with ease await them."
translations.idiomatic: We should train troops, stock armor, and wait at leisure for their move."

sentences.zh: 而頃興造殿舍，上下勞擾；

translations.literal: Yet recently raising and building palace lodges, above and below labor and disturb;
translations.idiomatic: Instead we exhaust the realm raising palaces;

sentences.zh: 若使吳、蜀知人虛實，通謀并勢，復俱送死，甚不易也。

translations.literal: if we let Wu and Shu know men's emptiness and substance, communicate plans and join strength, again together deliver death, it is very not easy."
translations.idiomatic: if Shu and Wu learn how thin we are stretched and strike together, the war will not be easily won."

sentences.zh: 昔漢文惜十家之資，不營小臺之娛；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han pitied ten households' resources, and did not build a small terrace for pleasure;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han refused a small terrace to save a few households' taxes;

sentences.zh: 去病慮匈奴之害，不遑治第之事。

translations.literal: Huo Qubing worried about the Xiongnu's harm, and had no leisure to manage building a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Qubing ignored his own mansion while the Xiongnu threatened the frontier.

sentences.zh: 況今所損者非惟百金之費，所憂者非徒北狄之患乎？

translations.literal: How much more what is lost now is not only a hundred gold in expense, what is worried about is not merely the northern Di's trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: Our waste runs far beyond a hundred pounds of gold, and the danger is not only the northern tribes."

sentences.zh: 可粗成見所營立，以充朝宴之儀。

translations.literal: It is possible roughly to complete what is seen built and established, to supply the court banquet's observances.
translations.idiomatic: Finish only what is already half built—enough for court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 訖罷作者，使得就農。

translations.literal: Finish and dismiss the workers, enabling them to return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Then dismiss the corvée gangs so they can go back to the fields.

sentences.zh: 二方平定，復可徐興。

translations.literal: When the two regions are pacified, again it is possible slowly to raise new works."
translations.idiomatic: When the two enemy states fall, you can build at leisure."

sentences.zh: 昔軒轅以二十五子，傳祚彌遠；

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Thearch with twenty-five sons, transmitting the mandate grew ever more distant;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Thearch had twenty-five sons and his line ran long;

sentences.zh: 周室以姬國四十，歷年滋多。

translations.literal: the Zhou house with forty Ji states, passing years became ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: the house of Zhou ruled through forty Ji principalities and lasted many centuries.

sentences.zh: 陛下聦達，窮理盡性，而頃皇子連多夭逝，熊羆之祥又未感應。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is intelligent and penetrating, exhausts pattern and completes nature, yet recently princes repeatedly for the most part died young, and the auspicious bear-and-pi sign has again not responded.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is wise as Heaven, yet princes keep dying in infancy and the omen of the "bear in the bedchamber" has not come.

sentences.zh: 羣下之心，莫不悒戚。

translations.literal: The hearts of the crowd below, none are not depressed and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Every official beneath you grieves in silence.

sentences.zh: 周禮，天子后妃以下百二十人，嬪嬙之儀，旣以盛矣。

translations.literal: By Zhou ritual, from the Son of Heaven's empress and consorts downward there were one hundred twenty persons; the concubines' observances were already abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou ritual capped the harem at one hundred twenty women—already ample.

sentences.zh: 竊聞後庭之數，或復過之，聖嗣不昌，殆能由此。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately heard that the rear palace's numbers perhaps again exceed this; the sage heir not flourishing, perhaps can be because of this.
translations.idiomatic: I hear your inner palaces hold even more; that may be why the imperial seed will not take.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為可妙簡淑媛，以備內官之數，其餘盡遣還家。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject considers it fitting subtly to select virtuous beauties, to supply the inner officials' numbers, the rest entirely send back home.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a modest number of worthy consorts and send the surplus home.

sentences.zh: 且以育精養神，專靜為寶。

translations.literal: Moreover thereby to nurture essence and nourish spirit, taking quiet and stillness as treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve your strength in calm—that is the true tonic.

sentences.zh: 如此，則螽斯之徵，可庶而致矣。

translations.literal: If so, then the sign of the katydids may perhaps be reached."
translations.idiomatic: Then you may win the blessing of many sons promised in the Odes."

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「知卿忠允，乃心王室，輒克昌言；

translations.literal: 〉The Emperor replied, saying: "I know you are loyal and even, your heart is the royal house, always able to speak forthrightly;
translations.idiomatic: 〉Cao Rui answered: "I know you are loyal and speak for the throne;

sentences.zh: 他復以聞。」

translations.literal: hereafter again report by memorial."
translations.idiomatic: keep such counsel coming."

sentences.zh: 時獵法甚峻。

translations.literal: At that time the hunting laws were very severe.
translations.idiomatic: Court hunting regulations had grown brutally strict.

sentences.zh: 宜陽典農劉龜竊於禁內射兎，其功曹張京詣校事言之。

translations.literal: The Yiyang agricultural official Liu Gui secretly shot rabbits inside the forbidden enclosure; his merit clerk Zhang Jing went to the surveillance official and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui, chief of the Yiyang agricultural colony, shot rabbits inside the imperial preserve; his merit clerk Zhang Jing denounced him to the surveillance office.

sentences.zh: 帝匿京名，收龜付獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor concealed Jing's name, seized Gui and delivered him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withheld the informer's name, arrested Liu Gui, and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 柔表請告者名，帝大怒曰：「劉龜當死，乃敢獵吾禁地。

translations.literal: Rou submitted a memorial requesting the accuser's name; the Emperor was greatly angry and said: "Liu Gui ought to die—yet he dared hunt in my forbidden ground.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou asked who had accused him. The emperor thundered: "Liu Gui deserves death for hunting my preserve.

sentences.zh: 送龜廷尉，廷尉便當考掠，何復請告者主名，吾豈妄收龜邪？

translations.literal: Send Gui to the Commandant of Justice—the Commandant of Justice ought immediately to examine and flog; why again request the accuser's principal name—could I have wrongly seized Gui?"
translations.idiomatic: I sent him to your tribunal for torture—why demand the informer's name? Do you think I arrested him wrongly?"

sentences.zh: 」柔曰：「廷尉，天下之平也，安得以至尊喜怒而毀法乎？

translations.literal: Rou said: "The Commandant of Justice is the balance of All under Heaven—how can one by the utmost honored's joy and anger destroy the law?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou answered: "The commandant of justice is the scale of the empire—not even the sovereign's temper may tip it."

sentences.zh: 」重復為奏，辭指深切。

translations.literal: He again repeated the memorial; the wording's intent was deep and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: He resubmitted the memorial in blunt, forceful language.

sentences.zh: 帝意寤，乃下京名。

translations.literal: The Emperor's intention awoke, thereupon issued Jing's name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and released Zhang Jing's name.

sentences.zh: 即還訊，各當其罪。

translations.literal: Immediately returning to interrogate, each received his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The court retried both men and sentenced each according to his guilt.

sentences.zh: 時制，吏遭大喪者，百日後皆給役。

translations.literal: At that time the regulation: clerks who met great mourning, after a hundred days all were supplied for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, clerks who had buried a parent were drafted for service after only a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 有司徒吏解弘遭父喪，後有軍事，受勑當行，以疾病為辭。

translations.literal: There was a Steward's Bureau clerk Xie Hong who met his father's mourning; afterward there was military affairs; receiving orders he ought to go, and used illness as excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hong of the Steward's Bureau was still mourning his father when a military levy arrived; he pleaded sickness to stay home.

sentences.zh: 詔怒曰：「汝非曾、閔，何言毀邪？

translations.literal: The edict angrily said: "You are not Zeng or Min—why speak of destruction?"
translations.idiomatic: An edict snapped: "You are no Zengzi or Min Ziqian—how dare you hide behind filial piety?"

sentences.zh: 」促收考竟。

translations.literal: Urge seize and investigate to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him seized and tortured to death.

sentences.zh: 柔見弘信甚羸劣，奏陳其事，宜加寬貸。

translations.literal: Rou saw Hong's trustworthiness was very weak and frail, memorialized stating the affair, and considered it fitting to add lenient forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou saw that Xie Hong was genuinely ill and asked clemency.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔曰：「孝哉弘也！

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict saying: "How filial Hong is!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, "This is true filial devotion!

sentences.zh: 其原之。」

translations.literal: Let him be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Release him."

sentences.zh: 初，公孫淵兄晃，為叔父恭任內侍，先淵未反，數陳其變。

translations.literal: At first, Gongsun Yuan's elder brother Huang, because his uncle Gong held office as inner attendant, before Yuan had yet rebelled, repeatedly stated his changes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gongsun Yuan's brother Gongsun Huang had served at court under his uncle Gongsun Gong and repeatedly warned that Yuan was turning traitor.

sentences.zh: 及淵謀逆，帝不忍巿斬，欲就獄殺之。

translations.literal: When Yuan plotted rebellion, the Emperor could not bear market execution, and wished in prison to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan rebelled, Cao Rui shrank from a public execution and planned to murder Huang in jail.

sentences.zh: 柔上疏曰：「書稱『用罪伐厥死，用德彰厥善』，此王制之明典也。

translations.literal: Rou submitted a memorial saying: "The document calls 'use punishment to attack their death, use virtue to display their good'—this is the clear canon of royal regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou quoted the classic: "Punish the guilty to the death, reward the good to make them shine"—the true royal standard.

sentences.zh: 晃及妻子叛逆之類，誠應梟縣，勿使遺育。

translations.literal: Huang and wife and children are of the sort of rebels and traitors, truly ought to be displayed on stakes, not letting them leave posterity.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel's kin may lawfully be strung on stakes and left childless.

sentences.zh: 而臣竊聞晃先數自歸，陳淵禍萌，雖為凶族，原心可恕。

translations.literal: Yet your subject has privately heard that Huang formerly repeatedly on his own returned, stating Yuan's disaster's sprouting; although of a wicked clan, tracing his heart can be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huang came forward more than once before the revolt to expose Yuan's plot; wicked clan or not, his motives deserve mercy.

sentences.zh: 夫仲尼亮司馬牛之憂，祁奚明叔向之過，在昔之美義也。

translations.literal: As for Zhong Ni illuminating Sima Niu's sorrow, Qi Xi clarifying Shu Xiang's fault—in the past these were fine righteous acts."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius comforted Sima Niu; Qi Xi cleared Shu Xiang—antiquity honored such compassion."

sentences.zh: 臣以為晃信有言，宜貸其死；

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Huang truly had speech; it is fitting to spare his death;
translations.idiomatic: I believe Huang told the truth and should be spared execution;

sentences.zh: 苟自無言，便當巿斬。

translations.literal: If he himself does not speak, then he ought to be executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: If he offers no defense, let him die on the public scaffold.

sentences.zh: 今進不赦其命，退不彰其罪，閉著囹圄，使自引分，四方觀國，或疑此舉也。

translations.literal: Now advancing does not spare his life, retreating does not manifest his guilt, shutting him in the prison, making him take his own portion—the four quarters observing the state may perhaps doubt this measure."
translations.idiomatic: You neither spare him as a reward nor publish his guilt as a warning—you only pen him until he takes his own life. Neighboring powers will ask what sort of justice that is."

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽，竟遣使齎金屑飲晃及其妻子，賜以棺、衣，殯歛於宅。

translations.literal: 〉The Emperor did not listen; in the end he sent an envoy bearing gold filings for Huang and his wife and children to drink, granted them coffin and clothes, and buried them at their residence.
translations.idiomatic: 〉The emperor would not hear of it. He sent a messenger with gold-dust wine for Huang and his household, then sent coffins and winding-sheets and had the bodies laid out at their home—execution dressed up as mercy.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：聞五帝無誥誓之文，三王無盟祝之事，然則盟誓之文，始自三季，質任之作，起於周微。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng says: I have heard that the Five Thearchs had no texts of oaths and pledges, the Three Kings had no affairs of covenants and prayers—if so, then the texts of covenants and oaths began from the three final ages, and the practice of hostage-giving arose in Zhou's decline.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Sheng remarks: the Five Thearchs swore no written oaths; the Three Kings cut no hostage treaties—such instruments belong to the decadent last three dynasties, and "pledge hostages" began as the Zhou house rotted.

sentences.zh: 夫貞夫之一，則天地可動，機心內萌，則鷗鳥不下。

translations.literal: As for the single integrity of the steadfast husband, then Heaven and earth can be moved; when calculating heart sprouts within, then gulls and birds do not alight.
translations.idiomatic: One utterly steadfast man can move heaven and earth; let cunning enter the heart and even the gulls will not land.

sentences.zh: 況信不足焉而祈物之必附，猜生於我而望彼之必懷，何異挾冰求溫，抱炭希涼者哉？

translations.literal: How much more when trust is insufficient yet praying that things must attach, when suspicion arises in oneself yet hoping the other must cherish—how is this different from hugging ice seeking warmth, embracing charcoal hoping for coolness?
translations.idiomatic: How much worse to lack good faith yet expect loyalty, or nurse suspicion yet demand devotion—as futile as hugging ice for warmth or clutching coals for coolness?

sentences.zh: 且夫要功之倫，陵肆之類，莫不背情任計，昧利忘親，縱懷慈孝之愛，或慮傾身之禍。

translations.literal: Moreover as for the sort who demand merit, the sort who act overbearing and reckless, none do not betray feeling and trust to calculation, be blind to profit and forget kin; even if they cherish compassionate filial love, some worry about the disaster of overturning self.
translations.idiomatic: Men who traffic in "merit" or swagger without restraint always choose calculation over feeling and profit over family; even when they mouth filial piety, they tremble for their own skins.

sentences.zh: 是以周、鄭交惡，漢高請羹，隗嚻捐子，馬超背父，其為酷忍如此之極也，安在其因質委誠，取任永固哉？

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou and Zheng exchanged malice, Han's Exalted Ancestor asked for the soup, Wei Xiao cast off his son, Ma Chao betrayed his father—their cruel ruthlessness reached such an extreme; where is there in this their relying on pledge and entrusting sincerity, obtaining trust forever firm?
translations.idiomatic: Hence the feud of Zhou and Zheng, Gaozu's "share the soup" threat, Wei Xiao abandoning his son, Ma Chao turning on his father—history is packed with such cruelty. Where is the "lasting trust" of hostages in that?

sentences.zh: 世主若能遠覽先王閑邪之至道，近鑒狡肆徇利之凶心，勝之以解網之仁，致之以來蘇之惠，燿之以雷霆之威，潤之以時雨之施，則不恭可歛衽於一朝，炰哮可屈膝於象魏矣。

translations.literal: If a ruler of the age can from afar survey the former kings' utmost Way of guarding against evil, from near mirror the crafty and reckless's evil heart of pursuing profit, overcome them with the benevolence of loosening the net, bring them with the favor of "come and be revived," dazzle them with the awe of thunderclap, moisten them with the application of timely rain—then irreverence can gather the lapels in one morning, roaring can bend the knee at the elephant gate.
translations.idiomatic: A wise sovereign studies the ancient kings' guard against treachery and the greedy tempers of his own day; he wins men with mercy, calls them back with kindness, overawes them like thunder, refreshes them like spring rain—then insolence can be folded away in a single court session and rebels can kneel beneath the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 何必拘厥親以來其情，逼所愛以制其命乎？

translations.literal: Why must one bind their kin to draw out their feelings, force those they love to control their lives?
translations.idiomatic: Why seize a man's relatives to squeeze out his loyalty or threaten what he loves to puppet his fate?

sentences.zh: 苟不能然，而仗夫計術，籠之以權數，檢之以一切，雖覽一室而庶徵於四海，法生鄙局，兾或半之暫益，自不得不有不忍之刑，以遂孥戮之罰，亦猶瀆盟由乎一人，而云俾墜其師，無克遺育之言耳。

translations.literal: If one cannot be thus, yet relies on those stratagems, cages them with schemes, inspects them with one-size-fits-all—although surveying one chamber yet hoping for auspicious responses from the four seas, the law produces mean narrowness, hoping perhaps for half a moment's benefit, from oneself inevitably there must be punishments one cannot bear, thereby to follow through slaughter of wives and children—it is also like breaking covenant through one man, yet saying "thereby cause his army to fall"—there is no wording of "none left to rear."
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot rule that way but lean on tricks, snare men with schemes, and police them with blanket decrees—if you hope to read the empire's mood from one closet while the law grows petty—you may win a moment's gain but you will inevitably reach for unbearable punishments, wipe out families, and call it justice—as empty as blaming one treaty-breaker and pretending no survivor was meant to remain.

sentences.zh: 豈得復引四罪不及之典，司馬牛獲宥之義乎？

translations.literal: How can one again cite the canon that the Four Crimes did not extend to kin, or the righteousness by which Sima Niu obtained pardon?
translations.idiomatic: How then can you invoke "the Four Punishments spared the families" or Confucius's pardon of Sima Niu?

sentences.zh: 假令任者皆不保其父兄，輒有二三之言，曲哀其意而悉活之，則長人子危親自存之悖。

translations.literal: Supposing those entrusted all could not protect their fathers and elder brothers, yet there were two or three statements, privately pitying their intent and entirely sparing them—then one lengthens men's sons endangering kin to save themselves perversity.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose every hostage who whispered a warning were spared for "good intentions"—you would only teach sons to sacrifice fathers to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 子弟雖質，必無刑戮之憂，父兄雖逆，終無勦絕之慮。

translations.literal: Sons and younger brothers though hostages, necessarily have no worry of execution; fathers and elder brothers though rebellious, in the end have no worry of extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Sons would hold hostage status as a license to rebel without fear of the block; fathers would plot knowing their boys could never be touched.

sentences.zh: 柔不究明此術非盛王之道，宜開張遠義，蠲此近制，而陳法內之刑以申一人之命，可謂心存小善，非王者之體。

translations.literal: Rou did not investigate and clarify that this method is not the Way of flourishing kings; it was fitting to open wide far-reaching righteousness and abolish this near regulation, yet he set forth punishments within the law to extend one man's life—this can be called the heart cherishing small kindness, not the body of a king.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou never explained that hostage policy is unworthy of a great king—that the throne should widen its principles and drop such petty leverage—yet he bent the statutes to spare one man. That is private kindness, not royal statesmanship.

sentences.zh: 古者殺人之中，又有仁焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity, within killing people there was again benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Even in antiquity the harshest justice could show humanity.

sentences.zh: 刑之於獄，未為失也。

translations.literal: Punishing him in prison is not losing the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Executing Huang in his cell would not have been unjust.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為辨章事理，貴得當時之宜，無為虛唱大言而終歸無用。

translations.literal: Your subject Songzhi considers that distinguishing and clarifying affairs' pattern, values obtaining what fits the time's suitability, not doing empty chanting of great words that in the end return to uselessness.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi holds that sound argument means what fits the moment—not lofty slogans that help nobody.

sentences.zh: 浮誕之論，不切於實，猶若畫魑魅之象，而躓於犬馬之形也。

translations.literal: Floating and reckless discourse, not cutting to the real, is like painting demon-spirit images yet stumbling on the forms of dogs and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Bombastic theory that never touches fact is like painting goblins and tripping over the shape of a dog.

sentences.zh: 質任之興，非防近世，況三方鼎峙，遼東偏遠，羈其親屬以防未然，不為非矣。

translations.literal: The rise of pledge-hostages was not guarding against the recent age; how much more when the three sides stand like a tripod, Liaodong is remote and partial—binding their kin to guard against what is not yet manifest is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hostages were never a modern invention; with three powers balanced and Liaodong far away, holding families as surety against future treason is hardly irrational.

sentences.zh: 柔謂晃有先言之善，宜蒙原心之宥。

translations.literal: Rou said Huang had the goodness of speaking first; it was fitting he receive pardon tracing his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou argued that Huang had warned the throne in advance and deserved clemency for his motives.

sentences.zh: 而盛責柔不能開張遠理，蠲此近制。

translations.literal: Yet Sheng blamed Rou for being unable to open wide far-reaching principle and abolish this near regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng faulted Gao Rou for not urging the emperor to scrap hostage policy altogether.

sentences.zh: 不達此言竟為何謂？

translations.literal: Not understanding what this statement finally means?
translations.idiomatic: What exactly did Sun Sheng mean by that?

sentences.zh: 若云猜防為非，質任宜廢，是謂應大明先王之道，不預任者生死也。

translations.literal: If you say suspicion-guarding is wrong and pledge-hostages ought to be abolished, this is saying one should clarify the former kings' great Way beforehand and not preside over life and death of those entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: If he meant "distrust is wrong, abandon hostages," he was asking the throne to proclaim high principle and stop deciding the fate of every pledge-holder.

sentences.zh: 晃之為任，歷年已久，豈得於殺活之際，方論至理之本。

translations.literal: Huang's being entrusted had already lasted many years—how could one at the juncture of killing or sparing suddenly debate the root of utmost principle?
translations.idiomatic: Huang had lived as a hostage for years; the moment of kill-or-spare is no time to reopen metaphysics.

sentences.zh: 是何異叢棘旣繁，事須判決，空論刑措之美，無聞當不之實哉？

translations.literal: How is this different from when the thorn-brake is already tangled, affairs require judgment and decision, yet empty discussing the beauty of putting aside punishments, hearing nothing of the reality of what is fitting or not?
translations.idiomatic: It is like a briar patch of lawsuits awaiting verdict while scholars drone about the idyll of "no punishments needed"—pretty words with no bearing on the case.

sentences.zh: 其為迂闊，亦已甚矣，漢高事窮理迫，權以濟親，而總之酷忍之科，旣已大有所誣。

translations.literal: That it is pedantic and wide of the mark is already extreme; Han's Exalted Ancestor, affairs exhausted and pattern pressed, used expediency to aid kin, yet lumping it in the category of cruel ruthlessness is already greatly false.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's lecture is hopelessly remote from the facts. Gaozu of Han bent the law under desperate pressure to help kin; to file that under "heartless cruelty" is simply wrong.

sentences.zh: 且自古已來，未有子弟妄告父兄以圖全身者，自存之悖，未之或聞。

translations.literal: Moreover from antiquity until now, there has never been sons and younger brothers who recklessly accused fathers and elder brothers to plot preserving themselves; the perversity of self-preservation has not been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: History offers no parade of sons who denounced fathers just to save their skins.

sentences.zh: 晃以兄告弟，而其事果驗。

translations.literal: Huang by elder brother reported younger brother, and the affair indeed was verified.
translations.idiomatic: Here an elder brother informed on a younger brother—and the warning proved true.

sentences.zh: 謂晃應殺，將以遏防。

translations.literal: To say Huang ought to be killed would be thereby to block prevention.
translations.idiomatic: Executing him would punish the very informant you need for frontier security.

sentences.zh: 若言之亦死，不言亦死，豈不杜歸善之心，失正刑之中哉？

translations.literal: If speaking also means death, not speaking also means death, how is this not blocking the heart of returning to goodness, losing the middle of correct punishment?
translations.idiomatic: If confession and silence alike mean death, you choke off repentance and abandon the mean of justice.

sentences.zh: 若趙括之母，以先請獲免，鍾會之兄，以密言全子，古今此比，蓋為不少。

translations.literal: Like Zhao Kuo's mother, who by first requesting obtained exemption; Zhong Hui's elder brother, who by secret words preserved his son—ancient and modern examples of this sort are probably not few.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuo's mother won exemption by petitioning first; Zhong Hui's brother saved a son with a secret plea—history knows many such parallels.

sentences.zh: 晃之前言，事同斯例，而獨遇否閉，良可哀哉！〉

translations.literal: Huang's earlier words, the affair matched this precedent, yet alone he met obstruction and closure—truly pitiable!〉
translations.idiomatic: Huang's warnings belong in that same class, yet he alone was silenced and destroyed—deeply to be mourned.〉

sentences.zh: 是時，殺禁地鹿者身死，財產沒官，有能覺告者厚加賞賜。

translations.literal: At this time, whoever killed the forbidden-ground deer suffered death personally, property confiscated to the government; whoever could detect and report received rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: At that time anyone who killed an imperial-park deer faced execution and forfeiture, while informers were richly paid.

sentences.zh: 柔上疏曰：「聖王之御世，莫不以廣農為務，儉用為資。

translations.literal: Rou submitted a memorial saying: "The sage king's governing the age, none do not take extending agriculture as their task and frugal use as their capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou wrote: "Every sage king made farming his first task and thrift his treasury.

sentences.zh: 夫農廣則穀積，用儉則財畜，畜財積穀而有憂患之虞者，未之有也。

translations.literal: When agriculture is extended then grain accumulates; when use is frugal then wealth is stored; storing wealth and accumulating grain yet having worry about disaster—there has never been such."
translations.idiomatic: Expand the fields and the granaries fill; tighten spending and the treasury swells—no dynasty that did both ever starved in crisis."

sentences.zh: 古者，一夫不耕，或為之饑；

translations.literal: In antiquity, if one husband did not plow, someone because of it went hungry;
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says: let one man skip the plow and someone goes hungry;

sentences.zh: 一婦不織，或為之寒。

translations.literal: if one woman did not weave, someone because of it went cold.
translations.idiomatic: let one woman skip the loom and someone shivers.

sentences.zh: 中閒已來，百姓供給衆役，親田者旣減，加頃復有獵禁，羣鹿犯暴，殘食生苗，處處為害，所傷不貲。

translations.literal: Since the middle period, the hundred surnames supplied many corvées; those who personally tilled the fields has already decreased; add that recently again there is a hunting prohibition, herds of deer invade violently, cruelly eating living sprouts, everywhere doing harm, the injury incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: Since mid-Han the people stagger under endless levies; fewer hands work the soil; now the deer preserves forbid hunting while the herds trample every green shoot—the damage is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 民雖障防，力不能禦。

translations.literal: Though the people try to wall and guard, their strength cannot resist.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers fence their plots in vain—the beasts overwhelm them.

sentences.zh: 至如熒陽左右，周數百里，歲略不收，元元之命，實可矜傷。

translations.literal: As for the area around Yingyang, for several hundred li in circumference, years for the most part reap no harvest; the black-haired folk's lives are truly pitiable and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Around Yingyang for hundreds of li the fields often yield nothing; the commoners' plight is heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 方今天下生財者甚少，而麋鹿之損者甚多。

translations.literal: At present under Heaven those who produce wealth are very few, while those harmed by elk and deer are very many.
translations.idiomatic: Too few hands grow food while too many deer devour it.

sentences.zh: 卒有兵戎之役，凶年之災，將無以待之。

translations.literal: Suddenly there are military campaigns, or famine-year disasters—there will be nothing wherewith to cope with them.
translations.idiomatic: When war or famine strikes, the state will have no reserves.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下覽先聖之所念，愍稼穡之艱難，寬放民間，使得捕鹿，遂除其禁，則衆庶久濟，莫不恱預矣。」

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty survey what the former sages pondered, pity the hardship of sowing and reaping, broadly release the folk, enabling them to capture deer, thereupon remove this prohibition—then the multitude will long be aided, none not pleased beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to remember how the sages cherished the harvest, pity the farmer's toil, lift the ban, and let the people cull the deer—then the realm will prosper and every household rejoice."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏名臣奏》載柔上疏曰：「臣深思陛下所以不早取此鹿者，誠欲使極蕃息，然後大取以為軍國之用。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei mingchen zou records Rou submitting a memorial saying: "Your subject deeply ponders why Your Majesty has not early taken these deer—sincerely wishing to make them extremely multiply, then greatly take them for army and state use.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Memorials of Wei Notables preserves another Gao Rou memorial: "I have pondered why Your Majesty lets the deer herds grow—to multiply them, then draft them wholesale for army and state.

sentences.zh: 然臣竊以為今鹿但有日耗，終無從得多也。

translations.literal: Yet your subject privately considers that now the deer only have daily depletion, in the end there is no way to obtain many."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the herds shrink every day; you will never harvest more by waiting."

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How do I know it?
translations.idiomatic: How do I know?

sentences.zh: 今禁地廣輪且千餘里，臣下計無慮其中有虎大小六百頭，狼有五百頭，狐萬頭。

translations.literal: Now the forbidden ground's circumference is nearly over a thousand li; your subject's subordinates calculate that without worry therein there are tigers large and small six hundred head, wolves five hundred head, foxes ten thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: The preserve spans more than a thousand li; my clerks estimate six hundred tigers, five hundred wolves, and ten thousand foxes within it.

sentences.zh: 使大虎一頭三日食一鹿，一虎一歲百二十鹿，是為六百頭虎一歲食七萬二千頭鹿也。

translations.literal: Supposing one large tiger every three days eats one deer, one tiger in one year one hundred twenty deer—this means six hundred tigers in one year eat seventy-two thousand deer.
translations.idiomatic: If each big cat eats one deer every three days, one tiger consumes 120 deer a year—600 tigers eat 72,000 deer annually.

sentences.zh: 使十狼日共食一鹿，是為五百頭狼一歲共食萬八千頭鹿。

translations.literal: Supposing ten wolves daily together eat one deer—this means five hundred wolves in one year together eat eighteen thousand deer.
translations.idiomatic: If ten wolves share a deer daily, 500 wolves polish off 18,000 deer a year.

sentences.zh: 鹿子始生，未能善走，使十狐一日共食一子，比至健走一月之間，是為萬狐一月共食鹿子三萬頭也。

translations.literal: Deer fawns when first born cannot yet run well; supposing ten foxes daily together eat one fawn, by the time they reach running strongly in one month's interval—this means ten thousand foxes in one month together eat deer fawns thirty thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: Newborn fawns cannot outrun a pack; ten thousand foxes eating one fawn each per day for a month devour 30,000 calves before they can bolt.

sentences.zh: 大凡一歲所食十二萬頭。

translations.literal: In rough calculation in one year what is eaten is 120,000 head.
translations.idiomatic: Rough annual toll: 120,000 deer.

sentences.zh: 其鵰鶚所害，臣置不計。

translations.literal: What eagles and kites harm, your subject sets aside and does not reckon.
translations.idiomatic: I leave raptors out of the ledger entirely.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，終無從得多，不如早取之為便也。」〉

translations.literal: Pushing by this, in the end there is no way to obtain many; it is not as good as early taking them as convenient."〉
translations.idiomatic: The arithmetic leaves no path to a larger herd—better to thin them now."〉

sentences.zh: 頃之，護軍營士竇禮近出不還。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, a guards camp soldier Dou Li went out nearby and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Dou Li, a man in the guards camp, left camp on an errand and vanished.

sentences.zh: 營以為亡，表言逐捕，沒其妻盈及男女為官奴婢。

translations.literal: The camp considered him a deserter, memorialized saying pursue and capture, and confiscated his wife Ying and sons and daughters as government slaves.
translations.idiomatic: His unit listed him as a deserter, asked for a warrant, and seized his wife Ying and children as government slaves.

sentences.zh: 盈連至州府，稱冤自訟，莫有省者。

translations.literal: Ying repeatedly reached prefecture and headquarters, stating wrong and suing on her own; none paid attention.
translations.idiomatic: Ying petitioned every yamen that her husband was no fugitive; no one listened.

sentences.zh: 乃辭詣廷尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon she took her plaint to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: She took her case to the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 柔問曰：「汝何以知夫不亡？

translations.literal: Rou asked: "By what do you know your husband did not desert?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou asked how she could be sure Dou Li had not run away.

sentences.zh: 」盈垂泣對曰：「夫少單特，養一老嫗為母，事甚恭謹，又哀兒女，撫視不離，非是輕狡不顧室家者也。

translations.literal: 〉Ying weeping replied: "My husband in youth was solitary and alone; he raised one old woman as mother, serving her very respectfully careful, and pitied sons and daughters, cherishing and watching without leaving—he is not the sort who is frivolous and crafty and disregards wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: 〉Weeping, she said Dou Li had raised his widowed mother with reverence and doted on his children—no flighty man who abandons kin."

sentences.zh: 」柔重問曰：「汝夫不與人有怨讎乎？

translations.literal: 〉Rou again asked: "Does your husband not have enmity with someone?"
translations.idiomatic: 〉"Did he have enemies?" Gao Rou asked.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「夫良善，與人無讎。

translations.literal: 〉She replied: "My husband was good and kind; with people he had no enmity."
translations.idiomatic: 〉"He was gentle and quarreled with no one."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「汝夫不與人交錢財乎？

translations.literal: 〉He again said: "Does your husband not with people exchange money goods?"
translations.idiomatic: 〉"Did he lend money to anyone?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「嘗出錢與同營士焦子文，求不得。

translations.literal: 〉She replied: "Once he lent money to a fellow-camp soldier Jiao Ziwen, and sought it without obtaining."
translations.idiomatic: 〉"He once lent cash to Jiao Ziwen of the same camp and could not collect it."

sentences.zh: 」時子文適坐小事繫獄，柔乃見子文，問所坐。

translations.literal: At that time Ziwen happened to sit because of a small matter in prison; Rou thereupon saw Ziwen and asked what he sat for.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Ziwen was in jail on a petty charge; Gao Rou had him brought in and asked what crime held him.

sentences.zh: 言次，曰：「汝頗曾舉人錢不？

translations.literal: In the midst of speaking, he said: "Have you perhaps ever borrowed people's money?"
translations.idiomatic: Midway through the interview he asked whether Ziwen had ever borrowed money.

sentences.zh: 」子文曰：「自以單貧，初不敢舉人錢物也。

translations.literal: 〉Ziwen said: "I myself considered myself solitary and poor; from the first I did not dare borrow people's money goods."
translations.idiomatic: 〉"I am too poor," Ziwen said, "to borrow from anyone."

sentences.zh: 」柔察子文色動，遂曰：「汝昔舉竇禮錢，何言不邪？

translations.literal: 〉Rou observed Ziwen's expression move, thereupon said: "You formerly borrowed Dou Li's money—why say it is not so?"
translations.idiomatic: 〉Gao Rou saw his face change. "You borrowed from Dou Li—why deny it?"

sentences.zh: 」子文恠知事露，應對不次。

translations.literal: 〉Ziwen marveled, knowing the affair was exposed; his answers did not follow order.
translations.idiomatic: 〉Ziwen realized the game was up and stammered.

sentences.zh: 柔曰：「汝已殺禮，便宜早服。

translations.literal: 〉Rou said: "You have already killed Li—it is fitting you early confess."
translations.idiomatic: 〉"You killed Dou Li. Confess now."

sentences.zh: 」子文於是叩頭，具首殺禮本末，埋藏處所。

translations.literal: 〉Ziwen thereupon knocked his head, fully stating killing Li from beginning to end, and the place where buried.
translations.idiomatic: 〉Ziwen kowtowed and confessed the murder and burial site.

sentences.zh: 柔便遣吏卒，承子文辭往掘禮，即得其屍。

translations.literal: 〉Rou then sent clerks and soldiers, following Ziwen's statement to go dig for Li, immediately obtaining his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: 〉Officers dug where he pointed and found Dou Li's body.

sentences.zh: 詔書復盈母子為平民。

translations.literal: 〉An edict restored Ying and mother and sons to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: 〉An edict freed Ying and her children.

sentences.zh: 班下天下，以禮為戒。

translations.literal: 〉It was promulgated under All under Heaven, taking Li as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: 〉The case was published empire-wide as a warning.

sentences.zh: 孫禮字德達，涿郡容城人也。

translations.literal: Sun Li, courtesy name Deda, was a man of Rongcheng in Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li, courtesy name Deda, came from Rongcheng in Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖平幽州，召為司空軍謀掾。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Youzhou, he was summoned as military planning aide to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao conquered Youzhou, Sun Li joined his staff as military-planning aide to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初喪亂時，禮與母相失，同郡馬台求得禮母，禮推家財盡以與台。

translations.literal: At the beginning of mourning and turmoil, Li and his mother were separated; a man of the same commandery, Ma Tai, found Li's mother; Li pushed his household wealth entirely to give to Tai.
translations.idiomatic: During the wars he lost his mother until a townsman named Ma Tai found her; Sun Li gave Ma Tai his entire fortune in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 台後坐法當死，禮私導令踰獄自首，旣而曰：「臣無逃亡之義。

translations.literal: Tai afterward sat for a crime deserving death; Li privately guided him to leap the prison and surrender himself; having done so then said: "Your subject has no righteousness of fleeing."
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Tai later faced execution, Sun Li smuggled him out to surrender, then declared that a minister has no right to live as a fugitive.

sentences.zh: 」徑詣刺姧主簿溫恢。

translations.literal: He went straight to the clerk for arrests chief clerk Wen Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He walked straight in to see chief clerk Wen Hui of the arrest bureau.

sentences.zh: 恢嘉之，具白太祖，各減死一等。

translations.literal: Hui praised him, fully reported to the Grand Progenitor, and each had death reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui praised both men and reported to Cao Cao, who commuted their sentences one degree.

sentences.zh: 後除河間郡丞，稍遷熒陽都尉。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed assistant to Hejian commandery, gradually promoted to Commandant of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Hejian assistant magistrate and rose to commandant of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 魯山中賊數百人，保固險阻，為民作害；

translations.literal: In the Lu mountains bandits several hundred men, guarding firm narrows, did harm to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of bandits held the Lu range and terrorized the district;

sentences.zh: 乃徙禮為魯相。

translations.literal: thereupon Li was transferred to be Chancellor of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li was named chancellor of Lu to deal with them.

sentences.zh: 禮至官，出俸穀，發吏民，募首級，招納降附，使還為閒，應時平泰。

translations.literal: When Li reached office, he issued his salary grain, mobilized clerks and people, recruited by head-count, summoned and received those who surrendered and attached, made them return as double agents, and in due time pacified and quieted.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his own salary on grain, mobilized troops and civilians, paid bounties for heads, accepted surrenders, and turned captives into double agents until the hills were calm.

sentences.zh: 歷山陽、平原、平昌、琅邪太守。

translations.literal: He passed through Administrator of Shanyang, Pingyuan, Pingchang, and Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as administrator of Shanyang, Pingyuan, Pingchang, and Langye.

sentences.zh: 從大司馬曹休征吳於夾石，禮諫以為不可深入，不從而敗。

translations.literal: Following Grand Marshal Cao Xiu on campaign against Wu at Jiashi, Li remonstrated considering it not fitting to go deep; they did not follow and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cao Xiu against Wu at Shiting and urged him not to advance too deep; Xiu ignored him and lost the battle.

sentences.zh: 遷陽平太守，入為尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted Administrator of Yangping, entered as Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to administrator of Yangping, then recalled to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 明帝方脩宮室，而節氣不和，天下少穀。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was repairing palace halls, yet seasonal qi was not harmonious, and All under Heaven had little grain.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Rui lavished labor on palace projects, the weather turned foul and grain grew scarce.

sentences.zh: 禮固爭，罷役，詔曰：「敬納讜言，促遣民作。

translations.literal: Li firmly contended, stopping the corvée; an edict said: "Respectfully accepting frank words, hasten to dispatch the people to work."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li protested until the emperor ordered the builders sent home "in respect for honest counsel."

sentences.zh: 」時李惠監作，復奏留一月，有所成訖。

translations.literal: At that time Li Hui supervised the work, again memorialized to retain one month, having something to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Li Hui then asked for one more month to finish the job.

sentences.zh: 禮徑至作所，不復重奏，稱詔罷民，帝奇其意而不責也。

translations.literal: Li went straight to the work site, did not again double-memorialize, declared edict and dismissed the people; the Emperor marveled at his intent and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li rode straight to the site, cited the earlier edict without waiting for a new rescript, and dismissed the labor gangs; the emperor admired his nerve and let it pass.

sentences.zh: 帝獵於大石山，虎趨乘輿，禮便投鞭下馬，欲奮劒斫虎，詔令禮上馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor hunted at Great Stone Mountain; a tiger rushed the imperial carriage; Li then cast aside whip and dismounted, wishing to raise sword and chop the tiger; an edict ordered Li to mount horse.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt at Great Stone Mountain a tiger charged the imperial carriage; Sun Li threw down his crop, drew his sword, and would have fought the beast until the emperor ordered him back into the saddle.

sentences.zh: 明帝臨崩之時，以曹爽為大將軍，宜得良佐，於牀下受遺詔，拜禮大將軍長史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming at the verge of death, because Cao Shuang was Grand General, it was fitting to obtain a fine assistant; at the bedside receiving the testamentary edict, he appointed Li Grand General's Chief Clerk, adding Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Cao Rui named Cao Shuang grand general and needed a strong chief clerk; he summoned Sun Li to the couch, appointed him chief clerk to the grand general, and added cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 禮亮直不撓，爽弗便也，以為揚州刺史，加伏波將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Li was bright and straight and did not bend; Shuang found it inconvenient, and appointed him Inspector of Yangzhou, adding General Who Crosses the Waves, granting the rank of marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li's blunt integrity irked Shuang, who shunted him off as inspector of Yangzhou with the title General Who Crosses the Waves and a secondary marquisate.

sentences.zh: 吳大將全琮帥數萬衆來侵寇，時州兵休使，在者無幾。

translations.literal: Wu's great general Quan Zong led several tens of thousands of troops to come invade and raid; at that time the provincial troops were on rest leave, those present were not many.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu general Quan Zong invaded with tens of thousands, most Yangzhou troops were on leave and few stood ready.

sentences.zh: 禮躬勒衞兵禦之，戰於芍陂，自旦及暮，將士死傷過半。

translations.literal: Li personally led guard soldiers to resist them, fought at Quebei, from dawn until dusk, generals and soldiers dead and wounded more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li led what guards he had to Quebei and fought from dawn to dusk until more than half his command fell.

sentences.zh: 禮犯蹈白刃，馬被數創，手秉枹鼓，奮不顧身，賊衆乃退。

translations.literal: Li trod the white blades; his horse received several wounds; he hand-grasped drumstick and drum, strove without regard to self; the bandit host thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He plunged into the blades, his mount was cut again and again, yet he beat the war drum himself until the enemy drew back.

sentences.zh: 詔書慰勞，賜絹七百匹。

translations.literal: An edict comforted and rewarded him, granting seven hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent him seven hundred bolts of silk in commendation.

sentences.zh: 禮為死事者設祀哭臨，哀號發心，皆以絹付亡者家，無以入身。

translations.literal: Li for those who died in the affair established sacrifice and wept over them, mourning cries issuing from the heart, all taking silk and paying the dead men's families, nothing entering himself.
translations.idiomatic: He held rites for the fallen, wept over the dead, and gave every bolt of his reward to the soldiers' widows—keeping none for himself.

sentences.zh: 徵拜少府，出為荊州刺史，遷兾州牧。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Junior Minister, went out as Inspector of Jingzhou, was promoted Shepherd of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as junior minister, sent out as inspector of Jingzhou, then raised to shepherd of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 太傅司馬宣王謂禮曰：「今清河、平原爭界八年，更二刺史，靡能決之；

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yi told Li: "Now Qinghe and Pingyuan have disputed the boundary eight years, having gone through two inspectors, none able to decide it;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yi said to Sun Li, "Qinghe and Pingyuan have wrangled over this border for eight years and outlasted two regional inspectors—no one has settled it.

sentences.zh: 虞、芮待文王而了，宜善令分明。

translations.literal: Yu and Rui waited for King Wen and it was finished—it is fitting you make good order and divide clearly."
translations.idiomatic: The lords of Yu and Rui waited for King Wen to draw the line; you must mark the boundary with equal clarity."

sentences.zh: 」禮曰：「訟者據墟墓為驗，聽者以先老為正，而老者不可加以榎楚，又墟墓或遷就高敞，或徙避仇讎。

translations.literal: 〉Li said: "In lawsuits they take ruined tombs as proof; those who hear the case take the oldest testimony as authoritative, yet old men cannot be beaten with mulberry switches, and again ruined tombs sometimes shift to higher dry ground, or move to flee enemies."
translations.idiomatic: 〉Sun Li replied, "Litigants wave grave mounds as evidence; judges defer to the oldest memory—yet you cannot flog octogenarians, and tombs migrate uphill or families relocate to escape feuds.

sentences.zh: 如今所聞，雖臯陶猶將為難。

translations.literal: By what is heard now, even Gao Yao would still find it difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Given such tangle, even Gao Yao would throw up his hands."

sentences.zh: 若欲使必也無訟，當以烈祖初封平原時圖決之。

translations.literal: If you wish to make certain there are no lawsuits, ought to use the cadastral map from when Emperor Lie (Cao Cao) first enfeoffed Pingyuan to decide it."
translations.idiomatic: If you want the suit to end, pull the survey drafted when Emperor Lie first created Pingyuan commandery and rule from that."

sentences.zh: 何必推古問故，以益辭訟？

translations.literal: Why must one push antiquity and rake up old precedents, thereby to increase lawsuits?"
translations.idiomatic: Why dig up ancient anecdotes only to feed new litigation?"

sentences.zh: 昔成王以桐葉戲叔虞，周公便以封之。

translations.literal: Formerly King Cheng with a paulownia leaf jested with Shu Yu, and the Duke of Zhou thereupon used it to enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng once teased his brother with a toy leaf "seal," and the Duke of Zhou turned the jest into a real enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 今圖藏在天府，便可於坐上斷也，豈待到州乎？

translations.literal: Now the map is stored in the imperial archive—then one can decide it from this seat—how await going to the province?"
translations.idiomatic: The true map sits in the imperial archive; you can settle the case from Luoyang—why send me back to the field?"

sentences.zh: 」宣王曰：「是也。

translations.literal: 〉Xuanwang said: "That is right."
translations.idiomatic: 〉Sima Yi said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 當別下圖。

translations.literal: 〉We ought separately to issue the map."
translations.idiomatic: 〉We shall have the archive issue the map."

sentences.zh: 」禮到，案圖宜屬平原。

translations.literal: 〉When Li arrived, examining the map it appropriately belonged to Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〉When Sun Li compared the charts, Pingyuan clearly held the disputed ground.

sentences.zh: 而曹爽信清河言，下書云：「圖不可用，當參異同。

translations.literal: Yet Cao Shuang trusted Qinghe's story, issued a document saying: "The map cannot be used; ought to compare divergences."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang sided with Qinghe and wrote back, "The archive map is unreliable—reopen the case."

sentences.zh: 」禮上疏曰：「管仲霸者之佐，其器又小，猶能奪伯氏駢邑，使沒齒無怨言。

translations.literal: 〉Li submitted a memorial saying: "Guan Zhong was a hegemon's assistant, his capacity again small, yet still could seize Boling district from the Bo clan, making them to the end of their teeth have no resentful words."
translations.idiomatic: 〉Sun Li shot back: "Guan Zhong was only a hegemon's minister, petty in talent, yet he could strip the Bo family of its Boling fief without earning a lifelong grudge.

sentences.zh: 臣受牧伯之任，奉聖朝明圖，驗地著之界，界實以王翁河為限；

translations.literal: Your subject has received a shepherd's charge, respectfully holding the sage court's clear map, verifying the boundary written on the land; the boundary truly takes the Wangweng River as limit;"
translations.idiomatic: I hold a governor's commission and the court's own survey: the line runs along the Wangweng River."

sentences.zh: 而鄃以馬丹候為驗，詐以鳴犢河為界。

translations.literal: "while Shu county cites Ma Danhou as proof, and fraudulently takes the Mingdu River as boundary."
translations.idiomatic: Shu county points to Ma Danhou and pretends the Mingdu River is the line."

sentences.zh: 假虛訟訴，疑誤臺閣。

translations.literal: "Borrowing empty lawsuits, confusing and misleading the ministries."
translations.idiomatic: They peddle perjury and clog the ministries with false claims."

sentences.zh: 竊聞衆口鑠金，浮石沈木，三人成巿虎，慈母投其杼。

translations.literal: "Your subject has heard that many mouths melt metal, floating stones sink wood, three men make a tiger in the market, a loving mother casts aside her shuttle."
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, slander melts metal, rumor floats stone, three men invent a market tiger, and even a fond mother drops her shuttle when the neighbors cry wolf."

sentences.zh: 今二郡爭界八年，一朝決之者，緣有解書圖畫，可得尋案擿校也。

translations.literal: "Now the two commanderies have disputed the border eight years; resolving it in one morning is because there are written explanations and drawings—obtainable to follow and check."
translations.idiomatic: Eight years of quarrel can end in one morning because we finally have maps and affidavits that can be checked against one another."

sentences.zh: 平原在兩河，向東上，其閒有爵隄，爵隄在高唐西南，所爭地在高唐西北，相去二十餘里，可謂長歎息流涕者也。

translations.literal: "Pingyuan lies between two rivers, trending east and upstream; between them is the Jue embankment; the Jue embankment lies southwest of Gaotang; the disputed land lies northwest of Gaotang, separated by more than twenty li—can be called long sighing with tears flowing."
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan sits between two streams that bend east; the Jue levee stands southwest of Gaotang while the contested fields lie northwest—more than twenty li apart. The fraud is enough to make an honest man weep."

sentences.zh: 案解與圖奏而鄃不受詔，此臣軟弱不勝其任，臣亦何顏尸祿素餐。

translations.literal: Examining the explanation and map memorialized yet Shu does not accept the edict—this is your subject's weakness being unable to bear the duty; your subject also with what face 'corpse salary' and eat plain?
translations.idiomatic: I laid the evidence before the throne yet Shu defies the edict—if that is my weakness as governor, what right have I to draw pay and eat idle rice?

sentences.zh: 」輒束帶著履，駕車待放。

translations.literal: 〉Then girding belt and donning shoes, harnessing carriage awaiting dismissal."
translations.idiomatic: 〉He belted his robe, laced his boots, hitched his cart, and waited to be cashiered.

sentences.zh: 爽見禮奏，大怒。

translations.literal: Shuang seeing Li's memorial was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang read the memorial and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 劾禮怨望，結刑五歲。

translations.literal: He impeached Li for resentful outlook, sentencing him to five years penal labor.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Sun Li for disloyal muttering and sentenced him to five years' hard labor.

sentences.zh: 在家期年，衆人多以為言，除城門校尉。

translations.literal: At home a full year, the crowd for the most part spoke on his behalf; he was appointed Colonel of the City Gates.
translations.idiomatic: After a year at home public opinion rallied for him, and he was named colonel of the city gates.

sentences.zh: 王觀字偉臺，東郡廩丘人也。

translations.literal: Wang Guan, courtesy name Weitai, was a man of Linqiu in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guan, courtesy name Weitai, came from Linqiu in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧勵志，太祖召為丞相文學掾，出為高唐、陽泉、酇、任令，所在稱治。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and poor, he urged his purpose; the Grand Progenitor summoned him as literary aide to the Chancellor, went out as magistrate of Gaotang, Yangquan, Zan, and Ren; wherever he was was praised as well-governed.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and destitute, he drove himself to study; Cao Cao took him on as literary aide to the Chancellor, then sent him out as magistrate of Gaotang, Yangquan, Zan, and Ren—each district praised his rule.

sentences.zh: 文帝踐阼，入為尚書郎、廷尉監，出為南陽、涿郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing, supervisor of the commandant of justice; went out as Administrator of Nanyang and Zhuo commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne Wang Guan entered the Masters of Writing as a gentleman and supervised the commandant of justice's office, then governed Nanyang and Zhuo as administrator.

sentences.zh: 涿北接鮮卑，數有寇盜，觀令邊民十家已上，屯居，築京候。

translations.literal: Zhuo north bordered the Xianbei, repeatedly had raiding bandits; Guan ordered border people of ten households and above to garrison together, building beacon towers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo faced the Xianbei on the north and suffered constant raids; Wang Guan ordered households of ten or more to build clustered forts and watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 時或有不願者，觀乃假遣朝吏，使歸助子弟，不與期會，但勑事訖各還。

translations.literal: At times some who were unwilling—Guan then falsely sent court clerks, making them return to help sons and younger brothers, not giving a fixed rendezvous, only ordering when affairs were finished each to return.
translations.idiomatic: When farmers balked, he pretended to dispatch capital clerks to "help" their sons at home—no fixed deadline, just "return when done."

sentences.zh: 於是吏民相率不督自勸，旬日之中，一時俱成。

translations.literal: Thereupon clerks and people leading one another without supervision self-urged; within ten days, all at once completed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and villagers nudged one another along and finished every fort within ten days—no whip needed.

sentences.zh: 守禦有備，寇鈔以息。

translations.literal: Guarding had preparation; raiding ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The line was garrisoned and the raids stopped.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，下詔書使郡縣條為劇、中、平者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he issued an edict ordering commanderies and counties to classify themselves as severe, middle, or mild.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Rui came to the throne he ordered every commandery to rate its own burden as heavy, middling, or light.

sentences.zh: 主者欲言郡為中平，觀教曰：「此郡濵近外虜，數有寇害，云何不為劇邪？

translations.literal: The chief clerk wished to report the commandery as middle and mild; Guan instructed saying: "This commandery borders near outer barbarians, repeatedly has raiding harm—how can it not be severe?"
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk wanted to file Zhuo as "middling"; Wang Guan snapped, "We border the steppe and take raids every season—how is that not a heavy district?"

sentences.zh: 」主者曰：「若郡為外劇，恐於明府有任子。

translations.literal: The chief clerk said: "If the commandery is outer severe, I fear for the enlightened prefect there is nominating an imperial son (hostage)."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk murmured, "A heavy rating means the administrator must send a son to court as hostage."

sentences.zh: 」觀曰：「夫君者，所以為民也。

translations.literal: Guan said: "That which is lord is thereby for the people."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guan answered, "A magistrate exists for the people, not the reverse."

sentences.zh: 今郡在外劇，則於役條當有降差。

translations.literal: "Now the commandery is outer severe, then on corvée regulations there ought to be lowered gradation."
translations.idiomatic: A "heavy" label lowers our corvée quota—that is the law's reward for danger.

sentences.zh: 豈可為太守之私而負一郡之民乎？

translations.literal: How can one for the grand administrator's private sake betray the one commandery's people?
translations.idiomatic: How could I lighten the county's burden just to spare myself a hostage son?

sentences.zh: 」遂言為外劇郡，後送任子詣鄴。

translations.literal: 〉Thereupon he reported as outer severe commandery; afterward sent nominating son to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: 〉He filed Zhuo as a heavy frontier commandery and later sent his only son to Ye as required.

sentences.zh: 時觀但有一子而又幼弱。

translations.literal: At that time Guan had only one son and moreover he was young and weak.
translations.idiomatic: He had but one boy, still small and frail.

sentences.zh: 其公心如此。

translations.literal: His public heart was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his sense of public duty.

sentences.zh: 觀治身清素，帥下以儉，僚屬承風，莫不自勵。

translations.literal: Guan governed self pure and plain, leading subordinates by frugality; subordinates received the wind, none not self-urging.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and taught frugality by example; his staff caught the habit and policed themselves.

sentences.zh: 明帝幸許昌，召觀為治書侍御史，典行臺獄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming visited Xuchang, he summoned Guan as palace assistant secretary for documents, in charge of traveling headquarters prisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Rui moved to Xuchang he named Wang Guan palace assistant secretary for documents and put him in charge of the mobile headquarters jails.

sentences.zh: 時多有倉卒喜怒，而觀不阿意順指。

translations.literal: At the time there were many hasty joys and angers, yet Guan did not curry favor by following directions.
translations.idiomatic: The court mood swung violently, yet Wang Guan refused to trim his opinions to please.

sentences.zh: 太尉司馬宣王請觀為從事中郎，遷為尚書，出為河南尹，徙少府。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Sima Yi requested Guan as senior clerk, promoted him to Master of Writing, sent him out as Administrator of Henan, transferred him to Junior Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi recruited him as senior clerk, then promoted him to Master of Writing, governor of Henan, and junior minister.

sentences.zh: 大將軍曹爽使材官張達斫家屋材，及諸私用之物，觀聞知，皆錄奪以沒官。

translations.literal: Grand General Cao Shuang had engineer Zhang Da chop house timber materials, reaching various things for private use; Guan hearing, all recorded and seized to confiscate to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang had engineer Zhang Da strip timber from Wang Guan's house for private building; Wang Guan seized every stick and impounded it for the state.

sentences.zh: 少府統三尚方御府內藏玩弄之寶，爽等奢放，多有干求，憚觀守法，乃徙為太僕。

translations.literal: The Junior Minister oversees the three Shangfang workshops, the imperial treasury, and inner storehouse plaything treasures; Shuang and others were extravagant and libertine, having many improper requests; fearing Guan upholding law, they transferred him to Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: The junior minister controlled the imperial workshops and inner treasuries; Shuang and his clique lived lavishly and hated a man who enforced the rules, so they kicked Wang Guan upstairs to grand coachman—a sinceure.

sentences.zh: 司馬宣王誅爽，使觀行中領軍，據爽弟羲營，賜爵關內侯，復為尚書，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Sima Yi executed Shuang, he sent Guan acting central leader of the garrison, occupying Shuang's younger brother Xi's camp, granted rank marquis within the passes, again Master of Writing, adding chief of horse for the consort carriages.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi struck down Shuang he sent Wang Guan as acting central camp commander to seize Cao Xi's barracks, enfeoffed him as a secondary marquis, restored him to Master of Writing, and added chief of horse for the consort carriages.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公即位，封中鄉亭侯。

translations.literal: When Noble Village Duke ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Mao took the throne Wang Guan received the village marquisate of Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，加光祿大夫，轉為右僕射。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, added Grand Counselor of the Household, transferred to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added grand counselor of the household and shifted to right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 常道鄉公即位，進封陽鄉侯，增邑千戶，并前二千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Duke of Changdao ascended the throne, his enfeoffment was advanced to village marquis of Yangxiang, increasing fief by one thousand households, together with previous making two thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Huan succeeded, Wang Guan was promoted to village marquis of Yangxiang with another thousand households, for 2,500 in all.

sentences.zh: 遷司空，固辭，不許，遣使即第拜授。

translations.literal: He was promoted Minister of Works, firmly declined, was not permitted, an envoy was sent to his residence to confer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was named minister of works, declined repeatedly, was refused permission to retire, and received the seal at his own door.

sentences.zh: 就官數日，上送印綬，輒自輿歸里舍。

translations.literal: Having taken office several days, he upward sent seals and ribbons, then by his own sedan chair returned to village residence.
translations.idiomatic: After a few days in office he returned the seal by litter and went home.

sentences.zh: 薨于家，遺令藏足容棺，不設明器，不封不樹。

translations.literal: He died at home; testamentary orders: vault only enough to contain coffin, not set out bright vessels, no mound no tree.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, ordering a pit only wide enough for the coffin, no grave goods, no mound, no marker tree.

sentences.zh: 謚曰肅侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Marquis Su ("the austere").

sentences.zh: 子悝嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Kui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 咸熈中，開建五等，以觀著勳前朝，改封悝膠東子。

translations.literal: In Xianxi, opening establishment of five ranks, because Guan displayed merit in the prior court, changed enfeoffment: Kui as secondary marquis of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks were established in the Xianxi era, Wang Guan's service to the former Wei court won Wang Kui a demotion in name to secondary marquis of Jiaodong under the new Jin system.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: 【Historian's appraisal】

sentences.zh: 評曰：韓曁處以靜居行化，出以任職流稱；

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Han Ji in stillness dwelt and practiced transformation; out he held office and flowed with praise;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Han Ji taught by quiet example at home and won renown in every post abroad;

sentences.zh: 崔林簡樸知能；

translations.literal: Cui Lin was plain and simple and knew capacity;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin was spare, honest, and shrewd in judging men;

sentences.zh: 高柔明於法理；

translations.literal: Gao Rou was clear on legal pattern;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou mastered the statutes and applied them with an even hand.

sentences.zh: 孫禮剛斷伉厲；

translations.literal: Sun Li was firm in decision and upright fierce;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li was resolute, blunt, and fearless;

sentences.zh: 王觀清勁貞白：咸克致公輔。

translations.literal: Wang Guan was pure, forceful, chaste, and white: all were able to reach the duke's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guan was incorruptible, stern, and spotless: each rose to steady the state at the highest level.

sentences.zh: 及曁年過八十，起家就列；

translations.literal: Reaching Ji passing eighty, from home he arose and joined the row;
translations.idiomatic: Han Ji passed eighty yet left retirement to take a minister's seat;

sentences.zh: 柔保官二十年，元老終位：比之徐邈、常林，於茲為疚矣。

translations.literal: Rou kept office twenty years, first minister to the end of position: comparing them to Xu Miao and Chang Lin, herein there is shame.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou clung to office for twenty years and died at the top of the ladder—set beside Xu Miao and Chang Lin, that record invites regret.
